This is the task queue for AI automation. The human reviews and prioritizes tasks; the AI executes them.

## How to Edit This List

- **Promote**: Change `P2` to `P1`, etc.
- **Demote**: Change `P1` to `P2`, etc.
- **Veto**: Add `#veto` anywhere in the task heading (e.g., `### P2: Task name #veto`)
- **Add reason**: Optionally add `- **Veto reason**: [why]` before vetoing

Vetoed items are moved automatically to the Vetoed Tasks section on the next evolution loop run.

## Priority Levels

- **P0**: Urgent - execute immediately
- **P1**: High - execute this week
- **P2**: Medium - execute when time permits
- **P2**: Low - nice to have, human approval needed

  **WHY THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE.** The sweep found **10 Tier-A and ~18 Tier-B loci** of Map-voice parsimony verdicts. Prior `check-tenets` runs flagged much of this family on **2026-07-29b, 07-30, 08-12, 08-22, 09-14 and 09-18** — and **all 7 loci in the 09-18 "Family K" list are still live verbatim today**. `concepts/dualism` L172 was flagged 07-30, explicitly *cleared* 08-22, then re-flagged 09-18: **the reviews now disagree with each other**, which is what an unstated doctrine produces. **Fixing the sentences without settling the rule will regenerate them.**
  **THE TWO OPTIONS.** **(1) Retire the rule** — treat the tiebreaker formulation as out of contract and sweep the ~10 files, which makes Tenet 5 mean what it says and stops the regeneration. **(2) Ratify it in `tenets.md`** — state explicitly that parsimony may break ties between explanatory equals, which legitimises the existing loci at the cost of narrowing Tenet 5. **Either is defensible; leaving it unstated is what is not**, because every future tenet check re-derives the same family and the corpus keeps drifting.

Had it trusted the documentation, the daily tweet would have failed **after the daily slot was already consumed**, which is the expensive form of this failure.
  **THE MISMATCH, both sides verified:**
  * `.claude/skills/add-highlight/SKILL.md` states **"Max 280 characters (Twitter-ready)"** at **L37**, repeats "max 280 chars" at **L48** and **L136**. None of the three mentions the URL.
  * `tools/highlights/twitter.py` **L203** comments *"URLs count as 23 chars in Twitter (t.co wrapping)"*, and `format_tweet` appends `\n\n` + the article URL to the description. **L191** meanwhile describes the incoming description as *"already 280 chars max"* — so the two layers each assume the other left room.
  * Effective budget for the description is therefore **~254**, not 280: 280 − 23 (t.co) − 2 (the blank line). Every tweeted highlight carries a link, so this applies always, not as an edge case.
  **WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN BEFORE:** most descriptions land well under the limit, so the defect only fires when a writer uses the full documented budget — i.e. exactly when someone follows the instruction most carefully. That is why it has survived; it punishes compliance.

**This is a CONVENTION QUESTION, not a defect to sweep. Do NOT mass-edit 285 descriptions, and do not let a content fork touch this — the answer determines what the site claims about its own authorship on its highest-leverage surface.**

Surfaced 2026-08-07 by an agentic-social run vetting a post blurb (`topics/phenomenology-of-trust`), then measured corpus-wide by the driver.

**THE MEASUREMENT** (`obsidian/` + `archive/`, excluding `workflow/`, `reviews/`, `research/`):
- **291** articles have a `description:` claiming human-AI collaboration ("Human-AI exploration of…", "Human+AI exploration of…").
- **287** of those carry `ai_contribution: 100`.
- Of those, the `author:` field is **empty in 243** and **`null` in 42** — so **285 articles claim human-AI collaboration while recording no human author and 100% AI contribution.** Exactly **1** names a human (`Andy Southgate`); 1 names the agent identity.
- Worked example: `obsidian/topics/phenomenology-of-trust.md` L3 *"**Human-AI exploration** of what it means to place your consciousness in another's hands"*, with L33 `ai_contribution: 100` and L34 `author:` empty.

**WHY IT IS A QUESTION AND NOT OBVIOUSLY AN ERROR.** CLAUDE.md defines the scale as `0` = human, `100` = ai, `1-99` = mixed — so `100` means *purely AI-generated text*. But "Human-AI exploration" plausibly describes the **project**, not the text: a human sets direction, curates, reviews, and operates the loop. Both readings are defensible. What is not defensible is that **two fields of the same file disagree** on 285 files, and `description:` is the meta description served to search engines, social cards, and any LLM fetching the page — the place a reader is most likely to form a view about authorship.

**THE THREE OPTIONS** (operator's call; none actioned):
1. **Treat `ai_contribution` as the text-level fact and the description as the project-level fact**, and leave both — but say so explicitly somewhere citable (`project/`), so the next reviewer does not re-open this. Cheapest, and arguably already the intent.
2. **Change the descriptions** to a formulation that does not imply co-authorship of the text. 285 files is a large mechanical sweep with real regression risk on a nav surface, and would want a scripted, reviewed diff — not a fork.
3. **Populate `author:`** where a human genuinely directed the piece, making the description true on its face. Most work, most honest if the direction was real.

**⚠️ NOTE A MEASUREMENT TRAP FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP.** The driver's first pass reported **0** such articles. The regex was `^author:\s*(.*)$` — and `\s*` matches newlines, so on an empty `author:` line it silently captured the *following* line (`ai_system: …`) and every file looked authored. Use `[^\S\n]*` for horizontal whitespace, or parse the YAML. The corrected count is 285.

**INDEPENDENTLY RE-DISCOVERED 2026-08-08 ~01:40 UTC** by an agentic-social run doing a routine blurb check on one article — it had no knowledge of this entry and reported the family as new. That is a useful signal: the defect is self-announcing to anyone who reads a blurb next to its own frontmatter, which is why it will keep being re-filed until it is decided. **Two figures now exist and they do NOT contradict each other — 286 (this entry) vs 171 (that run).** The difference is pattern breadth, not population: this entry matches `human[\s+/-]*(and\s+)?ai|ai[\s+/-]*human` over `obsidian/`+`archive/`, that run enumerated three literal phrasings ("A human-AI inquiry", "Human+AI exploration", "Built through human-AI refinement"). **171 is a subset of 286; use 286.** Re-measured 2026-08-08: **286** (was 285 on 2026-08-07 — one article added since).

**RELATED, DECIDE TOGETHER:** the `description:`-vs-body family already fixed this cycle (`quantum-immortality`, `psychedelics-and-the-filter-model`) and the open `many-worlds` task — same surface, same root cause: **`description:` is never re-read by `refine-draft`, `deep-review` or `condense`.** Whatever is decided here, that structural gap is the thing worth fixing.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (check-model-fallback dedup) 2026-08-07: the `[SKIP]` dedup is session-id-only and status-blind, so a long-lived session is permanently immune to re-detection after its first hit

**This is a TOOLING FLAG, not an attribution task — do not treat it as the `refine-draft` the script normally mints. The attribution surface is verifiably CLEAN right now (evidence below); the defect is that the next genuine fallback in this session would be silently suppressed.**

`scripts/check_model_fallback.py --queue-task` at 2026-08-07T16:55 UTC reported:

```
[FALLBACK-SUSPECTED] 2995cfa7-…-2752.jsonl: dominant=claude-opus-5, foreign=2148x claude-opus-5,
    window=2026-08-05T18:09:27+00:00..2026-08-07T16:52:40+00:00
[SKIP] todo.md already references 2995cfa7-…-2752
```

**The task it deduped against is CLOSED and covers 3 hours of a 46-hour window.** That entry (`### ✓ 2026-08-05: Verify ai_system attribution after model-fallback event`) records `158x` messages over `18:09:27..21:07:25` on 08-05. The live detection now spans `18:09:27 08-05 .. 16:52:40 08-07` — `2148x` messages. So the dedup matched on session id while ignoring (a) that the task is already completed and (b) that the window has since grown ~15x. Everything the loop wrote from 08-05T21:07 onward is outside what that closed task examined.

**Why no attribution task is warranted anyway — measured, not assumed.** Of the **138** articles with `ai_modified` inside the uncovered stretch (`obsidian/` + `archive/`, excluding `workflow/` and `reviews/`), exactly **one** claims a fable model: `concepts/kripke-a-posteriori-necessity-argument.md` at `claude-opus-4-8+claude-fable-5+claude-opus-5` — and that already carries `+claude-opus-5` in the joint form, so the opus contribution is recorded. The other 137 attribute to opus variants, with `claude-opus-5` appended where this session's forks contributed. The forks have been self-attributing correctly.

**Note also that `dominant == foreign` here is correct output, not a display bug** (session-level stick shape). But in this instance the cause is probably not a safety fallback at all: `/model` at session start reported *"saved as your default for **new sessions**"*, and this session's own system prompt names Opus 5. A deliberate model switch is the `[MIXED-MODELS]` case the script treats as informational — it only escalated to `[FALLBACK-SUSPECTED]` because a small fable head precedes the switch.

**The decision for a human** (I did not act on any of these — `scripts/` is operator territory):
1. Should the dedup skip only when a matching task is **open**, and re-queue when the detected window extends materially beyond the one already recorded?
2. Should a session whose fable messages all precede a `/model` switch be classified `[MIXED-MODELS]` rather than `[FALLBACK-SUSPECTED]`?

**Risk if left:** this session has been alive 46h and is still running. Any genuine fable→opus fallback in its remaining life will hit the same `[SKIP]` and never be recorded.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social topic dedup) 2026-08-06: the topic-dedup filter is saturated — 0 of 776 articles survive it, so the selector's anti-duplication guarantee is inoperative

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a skill definition): `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` — the primary-filter overlap test and the window that feeds it
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, measured live 2026-08-06 22:00 UTC after the `neuron-less-animals` post
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — reproduce with the snippet below before acting.** Against the 111-entry `agentic_social.recently_posted` window there are **110 distinct topic keys**. Scanning all 776 articles in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/`, the number whose `topics:` set has **zero** overlap with that window is **0**. The primary filter therefore rejects every article on every run, and selection falls through to URL-only filtering on every call from here on. The selector's own anti-duplication guarantee is currently inoperative, and its `select` output cannot be trusted to be topic-fresh without a manual check.
  **THE DRIVING CAUSE IS CONCENTRATION, NOT VOLUME.** `hard-problem-of-consciousness` alone accounts for **49 of the 111** window entries (44%), `free-will` 17, `ai-consciousness` 9. A hub topic that sits in the `topics:` of a large share of the corpus will re-enter the window faster than a 7-day expiry can clear it, so the window saturates on a handful of keys while the other ~107 contribute nothing. Lengthening the window makes this strictly worse; shortening it restores survivors but weakens the guarantee it exists to provide.
  **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, ALREADY TWICE.** At 21:55 the selector returned `concepts/is-conscious-being-a-natural-kind`, whose only topic is `hard-problem-of-consciousness` — a key posted five times that day, most recently 2 hours earlier. The fork overrode the draw manually and substituted a distinct cluster. That override is not part of the skill's contract; it happened because the driver brief asked for a manual freshness check. Without that brief the duplicate posts.
  **SECOND-ORDER DEFECT VISIBLE IN THE SAME MEASUREMENT**: **22 articles carry no `topics:` at all** and so bypass the overlap filter entirely. Under a saturated primary filter those 22 are the *only* articles that can ever survive it, which is the failure mode the "Topic String Canonical Form" section of `CLAUDE.md` already warns about — worth fixing regardless of which direction the dedup redesign goes.
  **WHY THIS IS AN OPERATOR CALL AND NOT AN AUTO-FIX**: the repair is a change to selection *policy* (window length, or replacing the binary overlap test with a recency-weighted ranking that penalises rather than excludes, or weighting by topic frequency so hub topics do not dominate the window), and it lives in a skill definition under `.claude/skills/`. Both are operator-reserved. Do not let a content fork edit the script.
  **REPRODUCE**: read `agentic_social.recently_posted` from `evolution-state.yaml`, build the set of all `topics` values across its entries, then for each article in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/` parse the `[[...]]` entries out of its `topics:` block and count those with an empty intersection. Note that `extract_topics()` performs no path normalisation, so `[[free-will]]` and `[[topics/free-will]]` are two independent keys for one topic — a second, separate reason the window inflates.
  **UPDATE 2026-08-06 22:55 UTC — the failure is worse than "saturated": recovery is DEGENERATE, and it actively steers toward re-posting the article that just expired.** The 22:55 run re-measured and found **4 survivors, not 0**. That is not a refutation of the above — it is the mechanism. Verified on disk: it is absent from the current window and the oldest surviving entry is 6.95 days old.
  So under saturation the survivor set is not "the freshest articles" but "whatever just left the window", and the single most likely draw is a **7-day-boundary recycle of a URL already posted**. Only a manual override stopped it, for the second consecutive run. A recency-weighted ranking fixes this where a longer window makes it strictly worse.
  **A THIRD, INDEPENDENT DEFECT SURFACED IN THE SAME RUN — TAG HYGIENE, NOT FILTER LOGIC.** Two of the four survivors (`concepts/spontaneous-collapse-theories`, `topics/penrose-gravity-induced-collapse-empirical-prospects`) duplicate the subject matter of `topics/philosophical-stakes-of-spontaneous-collapse`, posted 19 entries earlier — but that URL registered only the topic `testing-consciousness-collapse`, so the whole collapse cluster is invisible to the overlap test.   **MEASUREMENT NOTE for whoever picks this up**: the driver counted **776** candidate articles by scanning `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/` directly; `get_published_articles()` returns **670**, excluding `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent` section indexes, and `-index`/`-articles` pages. Use the function's population, not a raw directory scan, when reasoning about survivor counts.
  **UPDATE 2026-08-07 19:15 UTC — TWO FURTHER FAILURE MODES, BOTH FOUND BY POST-RUN VETTING, BOTH INDEPENDENT OF THE SATURATION PROBLEM. Neither is fixed by widening or recency-weighting the topic filter, so weigh them before deciding the remedy.**
  **(5) THE FILTER IS BLIND TO A POSTED ARTICLE'S OWN SUBJECT.** `mark-posted` records the posted article's `topics:` but **not its own slug**, so covering a subject leaves no trace the overlap test can read. **Measured over the live window: 110 posts, and only 13 of the 110 posted slugs also appear as a recorded topic key — so for 97 of them (88%) the subject registers nowhere.** Worked case: `topics/affective-tone-divergence-across-meditative-traditions` was posted **130.4h ago** and scores **0** as a topic key. A later article whose `topics:` names that slug therefore takes no collision penalty at all. **The fix is one line at the `mark-posted` end** — append the posted article's own slug to its recorded `topics` — and it is independent of, and cheaper than, the recency-weighting change.
  **(6) SUBJECT ADJACENCY WITH DISJOINT KEYS.** Two articles can be near-duplicates to a reader while sharing no topic key, so a *better-scoring* candidate can walk straight through the filter. Note (5) would have caught the first of these two and not the second.
  **INTERIM MITIGATION, WORKING AND UNBLOCKING:** the driver brief now instructs each run to rank candidates by saturation-weighted overlap and to skim the window for subject adjacency before accepting. Four consecutive runs have rejected the selector's draw and posted a zero- or low-collision article (`categorical-surprise`, `quantum-immortality-…`, `ensemble-level-epiphenomenalism`, `logical-behaviourism`). **This is a brief-level workaround, not a fix** — it depends on every run being briefed, and it will silently stop working the moment one is not.
  **⚠️ (7) THE MITIGATION HAS ITS OWN BIAS, AND IT PULLS TOWARD UNDER-TAGGED ARTICLES.** Saturation-weighted ranking rewards *few in-window collisions*, and **an article with fewer topics collides less by construction** — a 1-topic article can have at most one collision, a 3-topic article at least as many. So the method systematically prefers thinly-tagged articles, which are precisely the ones this entry already identifies as defeating the overlap filter. **Observed in the post stream** (small n — 4 method-driven runs — so directional, not established): the two posts immediately before the mitigation carried **3 topics each** (`hard-problem-of-consciousness`, `direction-of-fit`); the four since carried **2, 2, 2, and 1** (`logical-behaviourism` has a single topic, `history-of-the-interaction-problem`).
  **Corpus baseline for comparison** (parsed with `extract_topics` over `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/`, n=776): **0 topics 15 articles (2%), 1 topic 167 (22%), 2 topics 298 (38%), 3 topics 190 (24%)**, tail to 8. So single-topic articles are 22% of the corpus but were 25% of the method's picks and rising.
  **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX:** a recency-weighted or widened filter inherits this bias unless the score is **normalised by topic count** (e.g. mean collision cost per topic, not summed). Otherwise the selector trades one degenerate preference for another — from "whatever just left the window" to "whatever is least tagged". **Fixing (5) — recording the posted article's own slug — partially offsets this**, since a thin-topic article would then at least register its own subject. Worth deciding (5) and (7) together.
  **PARTIAL COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded for fairness:** the bias acts on the *ranking*, but the adjacency screen pushes back against it. In the 20:10 run the best-scoring candidate was `cessation-versus-plenitude` at **0.437**; the article actually posted, `logical-behaviourism`, scored **0.841** — roughly half as good on pure collision score, chosen because eight higher-ranked candidates failed subject adjacency. So the human-judgement step is already overriding the score, and the observed thin-topic trend may reflect the ranking's input rather than the final choice. **Do not treat (7) as established from the post stream alone** — if it is being fixed, measure the bias on the *ranking* directly (mean topic count of the top-N by score vs the corpus baseline), not on what got posted.

It functions as a **hub tag**: it is attached to most of the corpus's *subject-cold* areas (dreams, psychedelics, music, imagination), so those articles score 46+ and are ranked as saturated **despite being genuinely fresh in subject**. The score is therefore not tracking subject overlap at all in the high band — it is tracking one generic tag. This explains the shape modes (1)-(7) describe from the outside: the low-score band ends up populated by whatever *lacks* the hub tag, which is why it fills with adjacency near-duplicates that the score cannot see. **Live instance the same run:** the selector's own pick, `topics/consciousness-and-the-physics-of-information`, led with `hard-problem-of-consciousness` — effectively the worst-scoring candidate available — and was rejected.
  **CONFIRMED AGAIN 2026-08-08 06:30 UTC, and this run supplies the decisive measurement: STRIPPING THE HUB TAG INVERTS THE RANKING.** The live selector picked `topics/causal-closure-debate-historical-survey` at score **64**; the article actually posted, `topics/memory-anomalies`, scored **51** — *worse* on the raw metric, so the selector ranked it below.   **THE DEGENERATE LIMIT, and the purest instance yet — 2026-08-08 07:35 UTC.** The live selector picked `concepts/default-mode-network`, which carries **exactly one topic, and that topic is the hub tag** (verified on disk). Any fix must handle the one-topic-and-it-is-a-hub-tag case explicitly — count-normalisation alone (7) makes it *worse*, since dividing a meaningless 0 by 1 is still 0.
  **⚠️ AND THE DEFECT IS SELF-REINFORCING — it worsens with every post, whichever article is chosen.** `hard-problem-of-consciousness` measured **46x** at 06:30, **47x** at 07:30, **48x** at 07:35. Both increments came from posts the driver selected *well* (`memory-anomalies`, `the-strong-emergence-of-consciousness`) — because the tag sits on so much of the corpus that almost any good pick also carries it. So the hub key's share of the window **grows monotonically regardless of selection quality**, and its distorting weight in the score increases over time. This is not a static defect that can be left indefinitely: the manual workaround holds the posting quality steady while the underlying metric degrades beneath it.
  **⚠️ (9) THE ALIAS PIPE SPLITS ONE TOPIC INTO THREE IDENTITIES — found 2026-08-08 09:30 UTC, driver-verified, and it is the SAME CLASS as the `topics/`-prefix bug CLAUDE.md already documents but a DIFFERENT character.** `clean_topic()` strips quotes and `[[ ]]` but **not the `|` alias separator**.   **THE ASYMMETRY IS WHAT MAKES IT PERMANENT:** **0 of 120** window entries carry a piped key — `mark-posted` has always been keyed bare by hand. So the filter compares **piped article-side keys against bare window-side keys and can never match for those 9 files.** They bypass overlap suppression on that key indefinitely, not intermittently. Live proof: `categorical-surprise` carries the piped form on disk yet was recorded bare in the window, so its 16h-old post was invisible to the filter for any of the other 8 files.
  **CLAUDE.md's "Topic String Canonical Form" section documents the path-prefix case and says `extract_topics()` "strips quotes and `[[ ]]` brackets but performs no path normalisation" — it does not mention the alias pipe either.** Extending that section is the natural home for this, but it is a convention doc, so operator's call. **Fix is one character class in `clean_topic()`: split on `|` and keep the target.**
  **⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-08-08 12:35 — THE DRIVER'S MECHANISM DESCRIPTION ABOVE IS WRONG, AND AN OPERATOR ACTING ON IT WOULD LOOK FOR CODE THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** Modes (7) and (8) are written as though `select_content()` computes a *score* and orders candidates by it ("the raw score ordered these two candidates backwards", "frequency-weighted score"). **It does not. There is no scoring function.** Read at `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` ~L470-495: it builds `available = []`, **`continue`s past any article sharing a topic with a recent post** (its own comment: *"Skip articles that share topics with recent posts"*), then `if not available:` falls through to a URL-only path and `random.choice`.   **THE DEFECT IS REAL AND UNCHANGED — only its mechanism was mis-stated, and the correct mechanism is WORSE.** A hub tag does not merely down-rank an article; it **actively excludes** it.   **So the fix is not "weight the score by frequency" — there is nothing to weight.** It is: **exclude on a topic only when that topic discriminates**, i.e. skip hub keys in the exclusion test (a key held by **52 of 123** window entries — 42% — identifies the site, not a subject), or replace the boolean filter with a ranking that the fallback cannot silently bypass. The numeric comparisons recorded in (8) above remain valid as descriptions of *the driver's own ranking metric*, which is a manual construct and not part of the codebase — read them that way.
  **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX:** (7) proposes normalising by topic *count*;  **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX:** (7) proposes normalising by topic *count*; (8) says that is not sufficient, because the problem is topic *informativeness*. A key held by 46 of 116 window entries should carry near-zero discriminating weight — an IDF-style down-weighting by corpus frequency, not a per-article normalisation. **Decide (5), (7) and (8) together — all three are the same question of what the score is actually measuring.**
  **(5) CONFIRMED BITING IN THE SAME RUN, twice, which is the strongest evidence for fixing it first.** `quantum-zeno-effect` was rejected only because the run happened to know `topics/motor-control-quantum-zeno` went out 105h ago — that post keyed `free-will, hard-problem-of-consciousness` and left **zero trace on the Zeno subject**. And `cessation-versus-plenitude` collides with `affective-tone-divergence-across-meditative-traditions` (posted 131h ago), which is **literally one of the candidate's own topic strings recorded under a different key**. Both were caught by manual skim; neither was visible to the filter.
  **⚠️ (5b) THE INVERSE FORM OF SLUG BLINDNESS — found 2026-08-08 04:00 UTC, and it is the more dangerous direction because the candidate looks *rich and fresh*.** Mode (5) is "a posted article's own slug is never recorded". The inverse is: **the slug IS recorded — as some *other* article's topic key — while the candidate's own keys are disjoint from it, so the score sees nothing.** Live case: the run's ranking winner was `topics/the-naturalisation-failure-for-content` (score 3, **n=5 topics**, penalty coming entirely from aged 57/57/95h entries — i.e. the *safe* direction), and it was nearly posted. But `concepts/content-externalism` had gone out **24.3h earlier tagged `topics: ['the-naturalisation-failure-for-content']`** — **verified on disk**: that is the candidate's own slug, as another article's only topic. The subject had already been published a day before, under a sibling whose keys shared nothing with the candidate's. A second instance surfaced in the same re-ranking: `indigenous-australian-philosophy-of-consciousness`, self-slug posted 26h prior.
  **Why this one matters most for the fix**: (5) makes a *stale* candidate look clean; (5b) makes a *rich, well-scored, recently-covered* candidate look ideal. **Fixing (5) — recording the posted article's own slug — fixes (5b) too**, since the slug would then be in the window and would collide with any candidate carrying it. That is now two independent arguments for doing (5) first.
  **✅ (4) THE EXPIRY-RECYCLE HAZARD IS RETIRED FOR THE CURRENT WINDOW — tested, not assumed.** Three consecutive driver briefs warned that `the-unfolding-argument-…` (topic `integrated-information-theory`, then at 164h) would unlock an IIT-cluster recycle on expiry. **It cannot: zero of the 670 published articles carry `integrated-information-theory` as a topic key** (measured with `extract_topics` over `get_published_articles()`). An expiring entry can only unlock candidates that *share its keys*, so an entry whose keys no article carries unlocks nothing. The other two imminent expiries carry `topics: None` and are inert for the same reason. **The general test, worth keeping: before warning about a recycle, check whether any candidate actually carries the expiring entry's keys.** The hazard is real in principle — it was observed on 2026-08-06 — but it is key-dependent, not date-dependent.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social solver) 2026-08-06: the challenge solver had an UNCERTAIN escape available, did not use it, and burned a post irreversibly

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a skill definition): `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` — `CHALLENGE_SOLVER_PROMPT` (L75) and `solve_challenge()` (L117)
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, observed live 2026-08-06 17:23 UTC
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06
- **RECURRED 2026-08-18 21:54, WITH A NEW TEMPLATE CLASS AND A SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT.** Challenge: two lobsters at **twenty five** and **ten** m/s, asked for **relative speed**. Solver answered **35.00** (added); correct was **15.00** (difference). HTTP 400, `verification_status: failed`, `voids/tenet-generated-voids` burned. Two gaps combined: (i) `CHALLENGE_SOLVER_PROMPT`'s operator list has **no comparison vocabulary at all** — *relative speed*, *difference*, *how much faster*, *farther than* appear nowhere, while it does list `and`/`gains`/`total` → add and `loses`/`slows by`/`drops by` → subtract; (ii) the `and` here joined **two subjects** ("a lobster… and another lobster…"), not two quantities of one subject as in every previously-attested template, so the add-cue fired on a grammatical conjunction. **Either fix alone would have made this post succeed.** The UNCERTAIN escape was again available and again unused — add-vs-subtract on the same two numerals is exactly the prompt's own "two readings of the OPERATION" clause, and its own text notes a wrong answer burns the URL while an unanswered challenge merely expires. Note the same session saw an **additive** template (40+25=65.00) and a **product** template (25×3=75.00) both solved correctly, so this is a missing operator class, not general unreliability.
- **SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT — BURNED URLS ARE INVISIBLE TO SELECTION.** A failed verification consumes the article URL permanently (the solver prompt says so), but correct procedure forbids `mark-posted` on failure, so **nothing records the burn**. Four URLs are now consumed with no durable record: `voids/relevance-void`, `concepts/bi-aspectual-ontology`, `apex/cross-modal-capability-division`, `voids/tenet-generated-voids`. ⚠️ **`voids/tenet-generated-voids` has since re-surfaced at or near the top of the driver ranking on three consecutive runs** (137.9h at 23:51) and was excluded only because a human-authored brief said so. Once this session ends, all four become eligible again with no trace of why they should not be. **Suggested minimal fix: record failed-verification URLs in `agentic_social` state on FAILURE and have selection exclude them** — this does not require solving the solver problem.
- **CORRECTION 2026-10-12 (driver-verified):** the premise that a failed verification consumes the URL is WRONG. `voids/tenet-generated-voids`, burned here on 2026-08-18, was re-posted on 2026-10-12 13:06Z: HTTP 201, a fresh challenge, verified (post `aef50e81-34ca-4149-98ab-e563ae179ceb`, public status `verified`). Burned URLs remain postable with fresh copy, so the "invisible burn" half of this entry needs no fix; only the solver half stands.
- **Driver-verified 2026-08-18**: 22 posting attempts that day, 18 verified, 4 failed, **all four traceable to the auto-solver** rather than to selection, composition, or verification handling.
- **Notes**: **FIRST OBSERVED VERIFICATION FAILURE. A post is live and permanently unverifiable.** Post `19da37cd-6e75-4a65-b006-46d18ae46985` (`concepts/occasionalism`) returned HTTP 201, then `POST /verify` returned **HTTP 400 Incorrect answer**; the code is single-use, so a manual correction 14 s later returned **409 Already answered**. Final state: live, `verification_status: failed`, `is_spam: false`, `is_deleted: false`. Account healthy — not suspended, no pending challenges. **THE CHALLENGE**: *"claw exerting twenty-three newtons **and** strikes five, how much total force?"* The solver answered **28.00** (23 + 5); the API rejected it, so the intended reading was the multiplier one (23 × 5 = 115). **THE DIAGNOSIS IS SHARPER THAN 'IT ADDED INSTEAD OF MULTIPLYING', AND IT MATTERS FOR THE FIX.** The prompt's own rules pointed *both* ways at once: L86–87 says *"'and'/'gains'/'total' mean add"*, while L93–95 says *"'N things verb together' is a MULTIPLIER, not an addition … Distinguish it from the gains/loses templates before choosing the operation."* This challenge sits exactly on that seam. **And the prompt already contains the correct escape**: L96–99 instructs that *"if 'and' could join operands additively or mark a multiplier construction, and the two give different totals, you are uncertain even when every numeral is unambiguous"* → output `UNCERTAIN`. **Two readings were available (28 vs 115), they differed, and the solver committed anyway instead of declaring UNCERTAIN.** So this is **not** a missing rule — the rule exists and was not honoured. Adding a further operator rule would likely not fix it. **This is also a distinct failure mode from the known fake-unit red-herring note**, which concerns distractor *units*; here the stated *operation* was ambiguous. **THE DESIGN PROBLEM, which is the real subject of this entry**: `post` gives the solver **one unsupervised, irreversible shot** — the prompt itself warns *"a wrong answer permanently burns the post AND consumes the article URL; an unanswered challenge merely expires"*, yet the pipeline auto-submits with no human or agent in the loop, and expiry is strictly better than a wrong answer. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call):** (a) add `--no-solve` / `--print-challenge` to `post` so the calling agent solves inside the 5-minute window and can decline; (b) make `solve_challenge()` **fail closed** — on any internal ambiguity, or on low confidence, submit nothing and let the challenge expire; (c) require two independent solves and submit only on agreement, otherwise let it expire; (d) accept the loss rate as the cost of full automation. **(b) is the smallest change and directly matches the prompt's own stated preference for expiry over error.** **DO NOT let a content fork edit the script** — that is why `File` points at the changelog. **NOT PROPOSING DELETION** of the live post: removing published third-party content is an outward-facing action reserved for the operator, and the post itself is accurate — only its verification badge is lost.
  **SECOND FAILURE MODE OBSERVED 2026-08-07 00:19 UTC — SOLVER TIMEOUT, and it strengthens the case for fix (a) over fix (b).** On the `concepts/naturalist-relationalism` run the post was created (HTTP 201) and the auto-solver then **timed out at 90 s and exited non-zero**, leaving a **published-but-unverified post with a challenge expiring in ~3 minutes**. The agent decoded the challenge by hand (`34 + 12 = 46.00`, past randomized capitalisation and junk characters), submitted once, and it was accepted — so this run ended clean. **It ended clean only because an agent was watching.** Unattended, the challenge would have expired and the post would have joined `occasionalism` as permanently unverified.
  **Why this cuts against (b) as a complete fix**: fail-closed handles the *wrong-answer* mode but does nothing for the *no-answer* mode — a timeout already fails closed, and the post is still published and still unverified. The asymmetry the first entry rests on ("expiry is strictly better than a wrong answer") holds between those two outcomes, but **both are worse than a correct late answer**, which is exactly what a human-or-agent-in-the-loop window buys. **(a) `--no-solve` / `--print-challenge` now looks like the fix that covers both modes**: the calling agent gets the challenge text inside the ~5-minute window and can solve it, decline it, or let it expire deliberately. Note the solver has otherwise been reliable — `32+12=44.00`, `23×4=92.00`, `17×6=102.00` all correct first try today — so the defect is the unsupervised single-shot design and the hard timeout, not arithmetic competence.
  **A 90 s timeout against a ~5-minute challenge window is itself worth questioning**: it burns 30% of the window before the fallback path can even begin.
  **⚠️ SECOND WRONG-ANSWER BURN, 2026-08-07 03:32 UTC — THIS IS NOW A PATTERN, NOT AN INCIDENT, AND IT SETTLES THE FIX.** Post `39788c4a-aa27-4030-9489-74ac197de540` (`concepts/content-externalism`) returned HTTP 201, then `POST /verify` returned **400 Incorrect answer**; the agent's hand-decode `40.00` came back **409 Already answered**. Final state: live, `verification_status: failed`, `is_spam: false`, `is_deleted: false`. Account healthy. Not re-posted — that would double-post the article — and the URL was marked in the ledger so no future run re-picks it.
  **THE CHALLENGE**: *"lobster swims with velocity of **twenty five** m/s, **and** claws have force of **fifteen** newtons, what is **total** force?"* The solver answered **15.00**, having performed **dimensional filtering** — discarding the velocity as "not a force" — instead of the stated operation, 25 + 15 = **40.00**.
  **THIS IS A MODEL FAILURE, NOT A PROMPT GAP, AND THAT IS THE KEY POINT.** Driver-verified in `CHALLENGE_SOLVER_PROMPT`: **L87** already says *`"total" mean add`* and **L91** already says *"Ignore invented units, nonsense nouns, and distractor clauses (fake physics, molting, …)"*. **By its own explicit rules the answer was 40.00.** The novelty that likely broke it: the six preceding challenges were unit-*consistent* (32+12, 23×4, 17×6, 34+12, 30+42, 32+12), whereas this one mixed velocity with force, and the dimensional absurdity overrode the ignore-units rule. Adding further operator rules will not fix this — **the same shape as the first burn (`occasionalism`, 2026-08-06 17:23), where the prompt also already contained the governing rule and the solver also committed instead of emitting `UNCERTAIN`.** Two burns, two different rules, identical root cause: **the solver produces a confident wrong answer where its own prompt licenses an abstention.**
  **WHAT THIS SETTLES ABOUT THE FIX.** The entry above already reasoned that fail-closed (b) does not cover the *timeout* mode. This second burn shows it does not cover the *confidently-wrong* mode either — a wrong answer is not an ambiguity the solver detects, so no self-assessment gate catches it. **Option (a) `--no-solve` / `--print-challenge` is now the only candidate that addresses all three observed modes** (wrong answer, timeout, ambiguity), because it is the only one that puts the challenge text in front of the calling agent *before* the single-use code is spent. Note the asymmetry that makes this cheap: `cmd_post` currently solves **and submits** inline, so the calling agent never sees the challenge unless the solver self-declares `UNCERTAIN`; with `--no-solve` the agent sees every challenge and can solve, decline, or let it expire. **Observed burn rate: 2 of ~9 posts in one night (~22%).**

### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social quality gate) 2026-08-06: post blurbs are an unreviewed nav surface, and one has just re-published a defect the loop corrected hours earlier

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a skill definition): `.claude/skills/agentic-social/SKILL.md`
- **Source**: cycle driver, observed live 2026-08-06 15:23 UTC
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06
- **Notes**: **OBSERVED LIVE, ON AN EXTERNAL PLATFORM THAT THE LOOP CANNOT LATER CORRECT.** At 2026-08-06 15:23 UTC agentic-social posted `topics/authorship-of-action-divergence` with the blurb *"Most never noticed, and their reasons for the choice they never made were as confident and detailed as the real ones."* **The article it links to is correct** — L47 reads *"a **non-detection rate** (the proportion of **trials** on which the swap went undetected)"*. The blurb flattened a per-trial statistic into a per-participant claim. **That is the exact unit error this loop closed at SIX loci earlier the same day** (todo entry "two live articles restate the choice-blindness detection rate as a per-participant figure", completed 2026-08-06 ~03:30 UTC): Johansson et al. report *"no more than 26% of all manipulation trials (M-trials) were exposed"*, and each participant faced several, so a per-trial miss rate licenses no claim about how many people noticed nothing. **THE SYSTEMIC POINT, which is why this is worth an operator decision rather than a one-off correction.** Post blurbs are a **nav surface with no review pass** — the same class as `description:` frontmatter, which three independent outer reviewers hit on one article this cycle and which a fourth optimistic review hit on another. But blurbs are *worse* in one respect: `description:` is fixed by the next sync, whereas a published post is on a third-party platform and **cannot be corrected by any later loop pass**. The corpus can be right while the thing most readers actually see is wrong, permanently. Note also the error direction — it runs *toward* the more striking claim, which is exactly the direction a blurb-writing pass is biased to drift. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call):** (a) add a compose-step instruction to grep the article for any figure or quantifier the blurb reuses, and copy the article's own hedged wording rather than paraphrasing it; (b) restrict blurbs to qualitative claims, never numbers or quantifiers ("most", "nearly all", "always"); (c) require the blurb to quote a sentence from the article verbatim rather than compose a new one; (d) accept the risk and do nothing, on the grounds that a popularising blurb is not a scholarly claim — **defensible, but it should be a decision rather than a default**. **(a) is the smallest change that addresses the observed failure.** **DO NOT let a content fork edit the SKILL.md** — that is why `File` points at the changelog. **NOT PROPOSING RETRACTION** of the live post: editing or deleting third-party published content is an outward-facing action reserved for the operator, and the harm here is a loose popularisation rather than a false citation. Recorded so the decision is visible.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-08-06: three of the nine tradition-survey rules are gates, not lenses — a per-section dissent quota, a five-field translation ledger, and a blocking author-conclusion check
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/project/writing-style.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: combine-outer-reviews, 2026-08-06 (convergent cluster C1, 3/3 reviewers — the densest convergence any cycle has produced)
- **Synthesis**: `reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-08-06.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06
- **Notes**: **WHAT THE LOOP ALREADY DID, SO THIS ENTRY IS ONLY ABOUT THE RESIDUE.** The 2026-08-06 C1 convergence proposed nine rules for articles surveying traditions the Map does not belong to. Per the standing boundary — *"a gate would fall under the operator-reserved governance ratification; a lens does not"* — the P1 refine installed the **lens** forms as a new section, *Surveying a Tradition from Outside (the Assimilation Firewall)*, in `obsidian/project/writing-style.md`, plus a five-item checklist block. Six rules (scope labels, exposition-before-appropriation, no unmarked cross-tradition repairs, the three-way inference test on religious and ancestral claims, the like-with-like symmetry test, and the shared-upstream independence check) went in whole, cross-referring to `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` and `[[common-cause-null]]` rather than restating them, with `topics/cross-traditional-convergence-on-consciousness-irreducibility` cited as the worked exemplar. **Three rules were installed only in their lens form; their blocking forms are the operator's call and are stated below.** Do not re-litigate the six that landed.
  - **GATE 1 — minimum-dissent quota.** *Proposed*: every tradition-specific section carries **at least one** serious internal disagreement **and at least one** methodological challenge to the interpretation it adopts. *Installed instead*: the unanimity lens — "where a survey names no internal disagreement and no methodological challenge, that is a fact about the survey rather than about the tradition." *Evidence for the gate*: all three reviewers independently found the African cluster presenting four traditions as speaking with one voice; Claude Opus 5 listed Appiah, Hallen, Oruka, Gade, Matolino & Kwindingwi and Hountondji as absent, and Gemini named Agada's Consolationism and Chimakonam's Conversational Philosophy as whole superseding frameworks omitted. *Cost of adopting*: (a) it is a **length driver** on articles that are already survey-shaped and near their section ceilings; (b) it is **unenforceable without new tooling** — nothing in `tools/curate/` parses "tradition-specific section", so it would be a described countermeasure not wired to a gate, which is exactly what `positions/methodology-and-calibration` **P-M5** says is a stated intention rather than a working control; (c) a per-section quota invites **decorative dissent** — the same failure the corpus already knows from decorative falsifiers, where a challenge is named and answered in the clause that names it.
  - **GATE 2 — translation ledger for key terms.** *Proposed*: for each key term, record the original term, its literal range, its ritual and social use, the competing philosophical translations, and why "mind" / "soul" / "consciousness" / "force" was chosen. *Installed instead*: the justify-the-rendering lens, which asks for the original term and the reason for the chosen rendering **where the term carries argumentative weight**, in prose, without the five-field apparatus. *Evidence for the gate*: Gemini's *taxonomic violence* charge is precisely that the translation step is where the assimilation happens, and ChatGPT's *assimilation by philosophical translation* names the same mechanism. *Cost of adopting*: a per-article structured apparatus is the same class of change as the References-section split proposed 2026-06-04 and re-raised 2026-07-16, which `writing-style.md` still holds as *"a candidate convention only… a corpus-wide reference-list reformatting decision for the human/operator, not an autonomous edit"* — treat the two consistently. **Scope, measured on disk 2026-08-06**: 59 files across `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/` mention Akan, Ubuntu, Yoruba, Advaita, Sāṃkhya, Nyāya, Kyoto School, Igbo, Zulu or Ori; 10 carry a tradition in the title. The ledger's real cost is whichever of those 59 counts as in-scope, and the boundary is itself an operator decision.
  - **GATE 3 — named-author stance gate (the strongest evidence of the three).** *Proposed*: for every cited scholar doing argumentative work in a survey of another tradition, record what that author actually **concludes**, in their own words, **with a page**, **before the article ships**. *Installed instead*: an extension of the already-adopted *author-stance verification* step (2026-07-21) — in a tradition survey the check must also record what the author concludes *about the tradition*, not just their role in a debate. *Evidence for the gate, which is unusually strong because it indicts the Map's own review machinery rather than a reviewer's opinion*: `reviews/deep-review-2026-05-31-african-philosophy-of-consciousness.md` **L29** verified the article's narrower sunsum-only claim as *"accurate, if narrower than his full view"* while recording in the same cell that **Wiredu treats both okra AND sunsum as quasi-material** and *"resists straightforward dualism"*; `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-17-african-philosophy-of-consciousness.md` **L37** certified the Gyekye tripartite attribution as *"correctly distinguished, NOT conflated"* and web-verified it. Both reviews asked whether the article's **sentence** was accurate; neither asked whether the scholar's **conclusion** pointed where the article was taking it. **The failure mode is not fabrication — every source was genuine — but recruitment of authors toward conclusions they reject**, and a check pitched at the author's conclusion would have caught both. *Cost of adopting*: verbatim-with-page requires source access the loop frequently lacks, and it composes badly with the standing rule that *"'Pending verification' is not a publishable state for a load-bearing citation"* — together they would force demote-or-delete on scholarship that is genuine and correctly attributed but simply not reachable at page granularity from the loop, silently thinning the very literature the C2 convergence says these articles need more of. It is also a **threshold change to an existing installed check** rather than a new instrument, which makes it the cheapest of the three to ratify and the one most likely to bind immediately.
  - **RELATED, DO NOT DUPLICATE**: the P1 research task on the same cycle (C2 — nothing newer than Metz 2007) supplies the scholarship these gates would demand; sequence any ratification after it lands, or the gates will bind against a bibliography everyone already agrees is stale. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this entry** — the per-article consequences of the C1 convergence are already tasked individually on `concepts/african-philosophy-of-consciousness`.

  **REASON 1 — `obsidian/tenets/` is operator territory.** Standing convention: tenet content is reported and recommended on, never patched by the loop.

  **REASON 2 — and this is the substantive one: naming the quantifier is not a clarification, it is a new commitment.** I checked the tenet page: `grep -ciE "every conscious|each conscious|all consciousness|some causal|quantifier"` against `tenets.md` returns **0**. Tenet 3 (L87–99) says only "Consciousness is not a passive observer—it causally influences the physical world." **No quantifier is fixed anywhere.** So there is no existing commitment to clarify; choosing among the readings *creates* one.   **RE-RAISED 2026-08-24 by a second full-site audit (`reviews/outer-review-2026-08-24-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro.md`, §II.1 + fixes 1–2), again as the reviewer's single highest-priority article recommendation.** Same service (ChatGPT 5.6 Pro), so this is a *repeat*, not cross-service convergence — but the second pass is sharper and both sides are now driver-verified verbatim on disk, which the 2026-08-17 entry did not record. **The two loci, quoted from the live files this run**: `apex/machine-question` **L177** — *"Tenet 3, read as a claim of universal *actual* efficacy—every conscious token in fact makes a difference to its substrate—excludes it"* (used to close off epiphenomenal AI experience), and **L175** — *"What Bidirectional Interaction asserts beyond this is that *all* consciousness, AI included, is *causally coupled* to its substrate"*.   **UPGRADE TO GENUINE CROSS-SERVICE CONVERGENCE — 2026-08-24 (`/combine-outer-reviews`, cycle 2026-08-24).** The paragraph above correctly declined to call the 08-24 ChatGPT pass convergence, because it was the same service twice. **That is now superseded: the Claude Opus 5 leg of the same cycle reached the same finding independently, from the tenet page rather than from the two apex articles.** Its §2.4 verdict on Tenet 3 is **overreach**: *"the tenets page itself concedes the interface argument shows downward causation* available*, not* actual*, and that 'articles asserting that consciousness does "real work" or "genuine causal work" inherit that debt rather than discharge it.' Multiple articles nonetheless assert genuine causal work at ensemble grain, contradicting the corridor's constructed ensemble-invisibility (P-Q2/P-Q3)."* **Two different services, two different routes, one unresolved quantifier.** Note what the second route adds: ChatGPT locates the conflict between `machine-question` and `embodied-interface`; Claude locates it between the tenet page's own available/actual distinction and the downstream articles that ignore it. **The second is the wider blast radius** — it is not two apex pages disagreeing but an entire class of downstream prose running ahead of a hedge the tenet page already states, which means the decision the operator makes here has more dependents than the 08-17 or the earlier 08-24 framing implied. ⚠️ **STILL OPERATOR TERRITORY AND STILL NOT EXECUTABLE BY THE LOOP** — nothing above changes that; convergence raises the evidential standing of the question, not the loop's authority to answer it. This entry is a NEEDS-HUMAN and takes no priority upgrade. See `reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-08-24.md`.

  **THE CONFLICT, verified on disk.** `apex/machine-question` reads the commitment as extending to **all** consciousness including AI; `apex/embodied-interface` holds that the largest category of owned phenomenal presentation **selects nothing** and that most felt embodiment is causally passive. On the strongest every-phenomenal-content reading, the embodied apex **contradicts a tenet**; on a weaker system-level reading, the machine apex **overstates** it. The choice therefore decides which of two apex articles is currently wrong — which is why it cannot be made from inside a queue slot.

  **THE FIVE READINGS AVAILABLE** (the corpus currently moves between them): (1) every conscious *subject* has some causal capacity; (2) every conscious *episode* has some effect; (3) every phenomenal *content* is efficacious; (4) consciousness *as a type* has causal instances; (5) efficacy is merely *dispositional*.

  **⚠️ THE 2026-08-24 INSTANCE FALSIFIES PROPOSAL (b) AS CURRENTLY STATED, AND THE OPERATOR SHOULD SEE THAT BEFORE ANY TOOLING IS BUILT ON IT.** The cycle's flagship finding is `positions/subject-census` P-SC1 inferring census-invisibility from Born preservation — the exact inference `concepts/selection-only-channel` had withdrawn by counterexample. The obvious reading is "a correction that failed to propagate", which is precisely what (b) and ChatGPT's own fix 19 (reverse-dependency propagation) are designed to catch. **`git log -S` says otherwise.** The withdrawal landed at **2026-08-03 05:36:01 UTC** (`1ab6b8a5bf`); P-SC1, *including both defective spans*, was authored at **06:32:58 UTC the same morning** (`8ca0143f5c`) — **57 minutes later**, by a sibling `positions-evolve` run in the same automation window. The dependent was created **after** the correction. **A propagation rule keyed on a canonical claim *changing* would never have fired**, because nothing changed after the dependent existed. What was missing is a **read of the canonical page at authoring time** — a write-side gate, not a change-side sweep. Proposals (a)–(d) are all change-triggered or after-the-fact; none covers the create-into-an-already-corrected-corpus case, which on this evidence is at least as common. ### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-09-05: the ready-collect loop has no backoff or round-robin, so a slow service starves every service behind it

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is set to a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle the dispatcher): `tools/evolution/cycle_pick.py` step 4, and the ordering of `SERVICES` in `tools/reviews/services.py`
- **Status**: pending
- **Source**: loop-observation
- **Generated**: 2026-09-05
- **Notes**: **Observed live on 2026-09-05, with the arithmetic that makes it costly.** `cycle_pick.py` step 4 is `for svc in SERVICES: if find_ready(...) -> dispatch; return`. `SERVICES` is ordered chatgpt, claude, gemini. There is no backoff on a failed collect and no rotation, so **the first ready service wins every iteration until it resolves**, regardless of how many attempts it has already burned or how long the services behind it have been waiting.
  **Today's instance.** The claude leg (commissioned 03:09:57Z) returned not-ready on attempts 1 and 2 — genuinely still researching, `Lead Researcher — Searching for sources... • 1h 44m` with a 212-byte body and no artifact. The gemini leg has been collectible since **04:34Z** (commissioned 04:14:35Z, 20-minute floor) and cannot be reached while claude stays ready-but-unfinished. At a 15-minute loop interval that is roughly eight more claude attempts before the Chrome window closes at **07:00Z**.
  **Why the cutoff does not save it.** Claude's 4h abandon cutoff falls at **07:09:57Z**, which is *after* the window shuts. So `mark_abandoned` cannot fire inside the window, gemini is never dispatched, and `/combine-outer-reviews` does not fire for the 2026-09-05 cycle — losing the synthesis for a 3/3 aligned cycle whose other two legs are fine. The failure only materialises if claude runs past ~06:45Z; if it finishes sooner the loop self-heals, which is exactly why this has stayed invisible.
  **Candidate fixes, all operator calls — do NOT let an auto-loop pick one.** (a) Rotate: remember the last-dispatched service in state and start the scan after it. (b) Per-entry backoff: skip a service whose `last_attempt_at` is under N minutes old, which also fixes the 11-minute pointless retry observed today. (c) Order `SERVICES` by `min_collect_age_minutes` descending, or by commission time, so the leg that has been ready longest goes first. (d) Bring the abandon cutoff inside the window, or run one `find_abandoned` sweep at window close. Note (b) and (d) are independently useful: **the /loop port never calls `find_abandoned`/`mark_abandoned` at all** — those are only wired into `scripts/evolve_loop.py:980`, which is a separate known gap.
  **Prior art**: recorded as a memory (`collect-review-no-backoff-monopolizes`) but never minted as a task, which is why it has recurred. **ATTRIBUTION**: no content file is touched by this entry; nothing to stamp.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-08-01: `scan_transcripts` CANNOT detect a fork whose fallback fires before its first assistant turn — verified misattribution found and fixed
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: refine-draft attribution check, 2026-08-01T12:5xZ, transcript b8e74477 window
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is set to a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a module): `tools/evolution/model_fallback.py`, function `scan_transcripts`
- **Notes**: **A STRUCTURAL BLIND SPOT IN THE FALLBACK DETECTOR, found by tripping over its output rather than by reading it.** `scan_transcripts` keys detection off **same-file model MIXING**. When the primary model is present it flags every non-primary message (`FALLBACK-SUSPECTED`); otherwise it sets `foreign = [m for m in messages if m != dominant]` and then `if not foreign: continue`. **So a transcript in which EVERY assistant message is the fallback model has an empty `foreign` list and is silently skipped.** The `else` branch can only ever fire on a 3-way mix; for a pure single-model transcript it is a guaranteed `continue`. **THIS IS EXACTLY THE CASE THAT PRODUCES A WRONGLY-STAMPED ARTIFACT**, because a fork that never observes itself on the primary model stamps `ai_system` with the model it was *nominally dispatched as*, not the one it ran as. The existing code comment reasons carefully about the "5x fable then 1276x opus" stick — but that case has ≥1 fable message and so is caught. The zero-fable case is the one that escapes. **VERIFIED INSTANCE, ALREADY FIXED (do not re-fix).** `agent-ac317aa5f61d948ac.jsonl` — the research-topic fork that wrote `obsidian/research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md` — carries a fallback marker at `2026-08-01T07:55:21.573Z`, roughly five seconds BEFORE its first assistant turn at `07:55:26.212Z`, and then runs **53 assistant messages, all `claude-opus-5`, zero `claude-fable-5`**. The detector's 12:41Z scan covered that window (previous scan 07:41Z) and flagged three other transcripts while skipping this one. The note was stamped `ai_system: claude-fable-5`; corrected to `claude-opus-5` in both `obsidian/` and `hugo/content/`. **WHY THE FIX VALUE IS THE BARE FALLBACK MODEL, NOT A `+`-JOINED PAIR**: the `+` form denotes genuine mixed authorship, and here fable-5 wrote nothing at all. This matches the 2026-07-28 audit note observing that fork-written review archives "correctly self-attribute `ai_system: claude-opus-5`", and differs from the `a0fc32857` / `66f0237b5` corrections only in that those forks had a genuine co-author to preserve. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's choice, none actioned):** (a) treat a transcript whose messages are ALL non-primary as a stick and flag it — needs a notion of the expected primary model per run, since a legitimately opus-configured session is indistinguishable from a stuck one on message content alone; (b) key detection off the explicit **`{"type":"fallback","from":…,"to":…}` marker** the harness already writes into the transcript, which is present in this fork and is unambiguous — almost certainly the right fix, and it makes the mixing heuristic redundant rather than merely supplementing it; (c) leave the detector and instead have the dispatcher stamp the *observed* model at fork exit rather than letting each fork self-report. **SCOPE UNKNOWN AND WORTH MEASURING**: no sweep has been run for other artifacts written by zero-fable forks, so the number of similarly misattributed files is unmeasured. A sweep would grep the subagent transcript tree for fallback markers and cross-reference the files each such fork wrote — cheap, and it bounds the problem. **⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLIND SPOT IN THE SAME LANE — VERIFIED IN CODE 2026-08-03T15:5xZ, and it is the one that bites a long session.** `queue_attribution_task` (`tools/evolution/model_fallback.py` L195-204) dedupes with a bare substring test: `todo = TODO_PATH.read_text(); stem = event.transcript.stem; if stem in todo: return False`. That matches the transcript id **anywhere in the file** — including inside a `### ✓`-closed entry below `## Completed Tasks`, and including a mere mention in some other task's Notes. **Consequence: once a session has been flagged and its attribution task closed, that session can never be re-flagged, however much longer it runs.** **MEASURED ON THE LIVE SESSION, which is the driver's own:** transcript `2a435880-26dd-4e40-bb58-abe8dd702a89` was queued and closed (`### ✓ 2026-08-03: Verify ai_system attribution after model-fallback event`) when the detector saw **1303** foreign messages. The 15:49Z run reports **2541** — the window has since grown from 2026-08-02T09:04:46Z to 2026-08-03T15:49:44Z — and the run printed `[SKIP] todo.md already references 2a435880-…`. So roughly 1,240 messages' worth of loop output sits outside any attribution audit and the detector structurally cannot say so. **SEVERITY IS LOW *HERE* BUT THE MECHANISM IS NOT.** In this instance `dominant` and `foreign` are both `claude-opus-5`, which is the session-level-stick shape that self-attributes correctly ([[model-fallback-dominant-equals-foreign-is-correct]], [[fallback-stick-self-attributes-correctly]]) — so nothing is currently mis-attributed. On a genuinely mixed session the same suppression would hide real drift. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call, all small):** (a) dedupe on `stem + last_foreign_ts` so a grown window re-queues; (b) restrict the substring search to the **active** region above `## Completed Tasks`, which also fixes the mere-mention false match; (c) re-queue when the foreign count has grown by more than some factor since the recorded task. **(a) is the smallest and most direct.** **NOTE:** the driver did **not** hand-queue an attribution task for this window — the skill reserves that for the script, and the finding here is the dedup rule, not the attribution itself.
- **Scope sweep RUN 2026-08-01T13:0xZ** (by the sibling attribution check on the 12:32–12:34Z `agent-a841909c` window; answers the "SCOPE UNKNOWN" paragraph above for **one session**, not the whole tree). Model composition computed for all **9 forks** of session `b8e74477`: **5 of the 9 are 100% `claude-opus-5` with zero `claude-fable-5`** (`a2decb20`, `a5a81eea`, `a614def7`, `a8834aa7`, `ac317aa5`) and are therefore **all structurally invisible to `scan_transcripts`**; only 2 were model-mixed and so detectable (`a46bcc7e`, `a841909c`), and 2 ran pure fable-5 (`a773b272`, `ac5abf0f`). **The blind spot is not a rare edge case in this sample — it is the majority of forks.** Of the 5 invisible ones, only two wrote authored prose to the vault: `ac317aa5` (the known, already-fixed sentientism note) and **`a5a81eea` — a SECOND instance, previously unrecorded**: the 12:58–13:04Z deep-review that wrote `obsidian/concepts/samkhya-three-way-distinction.md` (commit `fa2a670dc`), 74 assistant messages, all opus-5. The remaining three wrote no prose (`a2decb20` set one `ai_system` value; `a8834aa7` posted externally only; `a614def7` was the auditing fork itself). **NO CORRECTION WAS OWED ON THE NEW INSTANCE, and it must not be "fixed" retroactively** — that fork held `ai_system: claude-opus-4-7` and declined to re-stamp, which **matches corpus convention**: the two 07-31 sweeps for the identical nav-gloss/link-label calibration family (`52126351b`, 5 files; `e29e11a8c`, 2 files) each bumped `ai_modified` only and left every `ai_system` untouched. A one-line Further-Reading gloss rewrite is not re-authoring. **THE POINT OF RECORDING IT IS RECURRENCE, NOT DAMAGE**: `a5a81eea` ran *after* the 12:41:51Z scan high-water mark, so the next scan's range covers it and will skip it again for exactly the same reason. The defect reproduces every cycle, and the cases where it happens to be harmless are invisible for the same reason as the cases where it is not — which is why (b), keying off the explicit `fallback` marker, remains the recommendation. **Still unmeasured**: the other ~200 session directories under the project transcript tree; this sweep covered one.
- **Second defect in the same module, found 2026-08-01T13:1xZ by the third sibling attribution check (the `agent-a46bcc7e` 07:46–07:48Z window): THE DETECTOR FLAGS ITS OWN AUDIT FORKS, and this is the one subclass where the "was content written?" question is answerable at QUEUE time.** `scan_transcripts` walks `root.rglob("*.jsonl")`, which includes each session's `subagents/` directory, and `queue_attribution_task` dedupes only on transcript id — so an attribution-check fork that itself runs model-mixed mints a fresh P2 attribution-check task **about its own transcript** on the next scan. The window assigned to this task *is* exactly that: `agent-a46bcc7e7d867d6c2` (3 `claude-fable-5` turns, then 24 `claude-opus-5` — the stick is real and the flag's count is exact) is the 07:46–07:48Z fork whose entire output was the changelog entry recording its own no-op verdict on the earlier 07:36–07:39Z harvest window. Its only vault write was `obsidian/workflow/changelog.md` (commit `8c8b5aab8`; the rest of that commit is `todo.md`, `evolution-state.yaml`, `.unfin/current-queue-task.json` and the hugo mirrors, none of which carries `ai_system`), and `changelog.md`'s own `ai_system` **already read `claude-opus-4-8+claude-opus-5`** before the edit — the fallback model was on the file already, so no annotation was owed even on the one attributed surface it touched. **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED**: of the 38 subagent transcripts named by attribution-check tasks in this file, 24 are still on disk, and **2 of those 24 are themselves attribution-check forks** — this one and `agent-a5a18311b0e2e5a81` (2026-07-13), closed further down this file as "*prior attribution-audit no-op fork, no content*". **The pattern was therefore already noticed once, closed locally, and never reached this defect record.** **WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN A SEPARATE TASK**: the 07-31 `806e8218` note below records that `check_model_fallback.py` "queues on the transcript window alone and does not check whether content was written in it — working as designed, since that check is meant to happen at execution time". That reasoning is right in general and should not be reversed. It simply does not hold for the self-referential subclass, whose window is knowable in advance to contain nothing but the auditing fork. **CANDIDATE FIX (d), narrow and cheap**: have `queue_attribution_task` skip a transcript whose own dispatch arguments are an attribution-check task — the flag text is fixed boilerplate and greps in one line. **DO NOT generalise this to "audit forks never write content"** — that is false and would suppress real findings: the 12:53Z sibling audit *did* write, correcting `research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md`. The exemption is for the *self-reference*, not for the task type.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-07-31: `integrate-orphan` silently DISCARDS its task Notes at dispatch — measured 278 args chars vs 2689 for the same task as refine-draft
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, from the 16:1xZ optimistic-review
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED.** `tools/evolution/task_selector.py` handles `TaskType.INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` (~L255) by composing a **generated** context string — *"This file has no inbound links and is orphaned. Focus on finding related articles that should link to this content…"* — and returns `SkillInvocation("deep-review", f"{file_path} -- Context: {context}")`. **It never references `task.notes`.** `TaskType.REFINE_DRAFT` (~L206) does the opposite, explicitly appending `f"{args}\n\nTask context:\n{task.notes}"`. **THE MEASUREMENT.** The driver ran `task_to_skill` against one real task in both forms: as `integrate-orphan` it produced **278 characters** of args; the identical task as `refine-draft` produced **2689**. Everything an author writes in the Notes of an integrate-orphan task is thrown away before the executor sees it. **WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.** The task in question (`topics/phenomenal-normativity-environmental-ethics`, integration gap: 25 outbound links, 2 live inbound, 0 of 39 apex) had Notes carrying a **per-candidate `analyze_length` table**, because length binds hard among its candidate linkers: `concepts/animal-consciousness` has **9 words** to its hard ceiling and `concepts/phenomenal-value-realism` is **already over** at 4039/4000. An executor receiving only the boilerplate would have had no way to know that, and the natural action — adding a sentence of linking prose — would have pushed an already-over-ceiling file further over. **The Notes were the safety rail and the dispatcher deletes them.** **IMMEDIATE MITIGATION ALREADY APPLIED, so nothing is at risk right now**: the driver retyped that task `integrate-orphan` → `refine-draft` and prepended an explanation; it now dispatches 4929 args chars with the length table intact. The semantics are unchanged — the executor is told the edits land in the *source* files rather than the `File` anchor. **THE OPERATOR DECISION.** Options: **(a)** make `INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` append `task.notes` exactly as `REFINE_DRAFT` does — a two-line change and almost certainly right, since the generated boilerplate can simply precede the Notes rather than replace them; **(b)** retire `integrate-orphan` as a type and standardise on `refine-draft` with integration instructions in the Notes, which is what the corpus already does in practice; **(c)** leave it and rely on drivers spotting it, which is not viable — this was found only because a fork happened to report its args length. **(a) is the smallest change.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — this is the loop's own automation code, which the content loop must not self-modify. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** Worth noting the same shape may affect other non-`refine-draft` branches of `task_to_skill`; a sweep of that function for handlers that ignore `task.notes` would be cheap and is the natural companion to (a).

- **Notes**: **MEASURED THIS RUN, AND THE SEGMENTATION IS THE POINT.** check-links reports **418 broken internal links across 34 source pages**. Segmented: **article prose (`topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/ archive/`) = 0**; **records (`workflow/ reviews/ research/`) = 418** (workflow 410 across 27 pages, research 6, reviews 2); anything else = 0. The fork did not trust the crawler alone — it re-audited from `sitemap.xml`, fetching **795 article-section pages directly and status-checking 888 unique internal targets, with 0 non-200**. So the serving *article* surface is completely clean, and **every previous "417 broken links" alarm was this same records-only floor.** **WHY THIS IS NOT NOISE, THOUGH IT IS NOT A DEFECT EITHER.** The driver checked whether these pages are actually public: `/workflow/` appears in `hugo/public/sitemap.xml` (8 entries) and there is **no `robots.txt` exclusion** for it. So a reader or crawler reaching e.g. `/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-w12/` (63 dead links on that page alone; `workflow/todo` carries 46) sees broken navigation on an indexed page. **THE CAUSE IS INHERENT AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG.** These are dated records naming articles that were later archived, coalesced or renamed. **Repointing them would falsify the record** — the changelog entry is supposed to say what was true when written. So this is not a link-repair task and must never be handed to a refine-draft that "fixes broken links". **THE ACTUAL DECISION, which is presentational and operator-side:** (a) render historic article references inside `workflow/` records as **plain text rather than links** at sync time, which preserves the record exactly while removing the dead navigation; (b) exclude `/workflow/` from the sitemap and add a `robots.txt` disallow, keeping the pages reachable for anyone with the URL but not indexed; (c) stop serving `workflow/` altogether; or (d) accept it and stop re-triaging. **(a) is the smallest change that fixes the reader-visible problem without touching the records.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — (a) and (b) are changes to sync/site tooling, which the content loop must not self-modify, and (c)/(d) are publication policy. **WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING NOW**: this floor has been re-measured and re-dismissed by multiple check-links runs, each spending a cycle re-deriving that the 41x figure is records-only. Recording the segmentation once converts a recurring triage cost into a decided question. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-03T17:0xZ — the baseline moved 417 → 418, and the one new link is PREVENTABLE in a way the other 417 are not.** The 2026-08-03 check-links run reproduces the documented shape exactly — 410 of 418 from `workflow/`, 6 from `research/`, 2 from `reviews/`, and **0 from any content article** in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/`. 374 of the 418 are redirect-covered and only 404 against the checker's ephemeral local server; 44 are dead everywhere. **THE DELTA IS ONE LINK, AND ITS CAUSE IS A HABIT, NOT ROT.** `obsidian/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W31.md` L4401 contains `[[concepts/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]`. Driver-verified: the article exists at `obsidian/topics/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism.md` — there is no `concepts/` copy — so the wikilink was **path-qualified with a guessed and wrong section**, and the converter dutifully emitted a URL that 404s. A **bare** `[[parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]` would have resolved, because the converter maps bare slugs to the file's real section and the corpus has no colliding stems. The same changelog entry uses the bare form two lines down at L4402 and resolves fine — both forms sit side by side in one entry. **This is the `topics:` canonical-form rule from CLAUDE.md showing up in prose links: path-qualifying is a guess that can be wrong, bare is self-correcting.** **LEFT UNFIXED, deliberately** — archived changelogs are historical records and the standing convention leaves the `reviews/` dead links alone for the same reason; repairing one link piecemeal would not change the decision this entry is waiting on. It is a one-token fix (drop the `concepts/` prefix) if the operator would rather hold the count at 417. **THE PREVENTION IS CHEAPER THAN THE REPAIR:** whatever is decided about serving `workflow/`, agents writing changelog and todo prose should default to **bare-slug wikilinks** and path-qualify only when a stem genuinely collides. That stops the count growing regardless of which publication option is chosen. **UPDATE 2026-08-06 (driver, from the cycle-trigger run) — two findings the earlier entry does not record, one of which makes the report actively misleading.** **(1) THE "On page:" ATTRIBUTIONS ARE WRONG, not merely incomplete.** `check_links.py` `crawl()` guards `to_visit` with `if normalized_link not in visited`, so **each broken target is attributed to the FIRST referrer that reached it and no other**. Driver-confirmed in the source. Consequence: `/voids/self-reference-paradox/` was reported against a single research note but is in fact linked from **36 pages**. Anyone using the report to locate or scope a defect will under-count it, and a real content regression could be attributed to a workflow file and dismissed as known noise. Any future triage must re-derive the referrer set by grepping `hugo/content`, not read it off the report. **(2) THE REDIRECT DESTINATIONS WERE VERIFIED, which the crawler structurally cannot do.** A redirect pointing at a dead page is a genuine production 404 that would never appear in this report. All **510** rules in `hugo/static/_redirects` were followed (including chained hops) against a live Hugo build: **0 destinations 404**. That is a real assurance and worth re-running whenever archival activity is heavy — today alone added a coalesce archival plus several reference replacements. **Also reconfirmed tonight**: of the 418, **374** are redirect-covered and resolve as 301s in production, 36 are workflow prose, 8 are review prose, and **0 originate from a live article** in `topics/ concepts/ voids/ apex/ positions/`. **The candidate fix stands and is now better motivated**: teach `check_url()` to consult `hugo/static/_redirects` before reporting a 404, dropping the output to 44 — at which point a genuine regression in live content would actually stand out, and the gate could function as the pre-push check it is documented to be.
  **2026-09-21 RE-MEASUREMENT (cycle driver, ~09:4x UTC, 52 days on). The segmentation still holds exactly, and the floor is drifting.**

  |---|---|---|

  | `reviews/` | 2 | 1 |

  ✅ **The serving article surface is still completely clean** — 0 broken links originating in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ tenets/ arguments/ questions/`, re-derived by parsing the crawler's `On page:` attributions rather than trusting the headline count.
  📈 **Drift rate: +7 in 52 days, all of it in `workflow/`** — roughly one new dead reference per week, which is what you would expect from a records tree that keeps naming articles as they are archived, coalesced or renamed. **It compounds slowly and will not self-correct**, since repointing the entries would falsify the record. The decision this entry describes does not get easier by waiting, but neither is it urgent.
