### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social config) 2026-07-31: the topic-dedupe filter is silently DEAD — 0 of 671 articles survive it, so every pick falls through to URL-only selection
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, from the 13:01Z agentic-social run
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the driver ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-07-31T13:0xZ and got: 671 published articles, 158 recently-posted URLs, 200 recently-posted topics, 514 articles surviving the URL filter, and *0* surviving the URL+topic filter.** **THE MECHANISM.** `select_content()` in `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` (~L475–L491) skips any article sharing *any* topic with the recently-posted set. The recently-posted window holds **158 posts carrying 200 distinct topics** — and because Map topic tags are broad and heavily reused (`hard-problem-of-consciousness` alone is applied across a large fraction of the corpus), that 200-topic union now intersects **every single article**. `available` therefore comes back empty on every run. **THE REAL PROBLEM IS THE NEXT LINE.** At ~L493 the code does `if not available:` and silently re-populates from URL-only filtering, with no log line, no warning, and no signal to the caller. So the skill reports a normal successful selection while the topic dedupe it advertises has contributed **nothing**. This is precisely the pattern `CLAUDE.md` forbids under *Error Handling* — "**Never use fallthrough logic that hides errors** … Do NOT provide a catch-all `else` that silently substitutes a default behavior." **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, not hypothetical:** of the six posts on 2026-07-31 before this was caught, **three consecutive** (09:27 `phenomenology-of-attention-to-absence`, 10:17 `stapp-quantum-mind`, 11:15 `integrated-information-theory`) carried `hard-problem-of-consciousness`, and the 13:01 run's `select` again returned a `hard-problem`-only article (`topics/quantum-darwinism-and-consciousness`) as its top pick — a fourth in a row. The last two runs only avoided it because the driver briefed the fork to check the tracked history by hand and enumerate the pool manually. **That manual workaround is not sustainable and should not become the fix.** **WHY THIS IS AN OPERATOR CALL RATHER THAN AN AUTOMATED ONE:** the remedy is a tuning decision with a real trade-off, and the loop should not pick it unilaterally. Options: **(a)** decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe but narrow *topic* dedupe to 24–48h, which restores the filter's bite while still preventing same-day repetition; **(b)** require overlap on *all* of an article's topics rather than any one, so a broad shared tag like `hard-problem-of-consciousness` no longer vetoes an otherwise-distinct article; **(c)** weight topics by corpus frequency and ignore the most common tags for dedupe purposes; **(d)** cap the topic union at the N most recent posts rather than the full window. **(a) is the smallest change and probably the right one.** **INDEPENDENT OF WHICH OPTION IS CHOSEN, THE FALLTHROUGH SHOULD BE MADE LOUD** — at minimum log a warning when the topic filter empties the pool, so a future silent degradation is visible rather than masquerading as a normal run. **DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY WIDENING THE POSTING CADENCE OR PRUNING `recently_posted`** — pruning would also weaken URL dedupe, which is working correctly and is the thing preventing genuine duplicate posts. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T14:4xZ — THE MANUAL WORKAROUND HAS NOW PRODUCED ITS FIRST MISS, WHICH STRENGTHENS THE CASE FOR FIXING THIS.** Because the filter is inert, the driver has been hand-supplying each run with the day's topic union and the fork has been enumerating the pool manually. That held for four runs and failed on the fifth. The 14:45Z post (`concepts/parfit-reductionism`) carries topics **`personal-identity`** and **`meaning-of-life`**. Both are correctly disjoint from the 24-topic union the driver supplied *for that day* — but **both recur repeatedly inside the ~7-day dedupe window the rule actually specifies**: `personal-identity` in 5 earlier posts, most recently **the previous day** (`narrative-coherence`, 2026-07-30); `meaning-of-life` in 5 earlier posts, also most recently the previous day (`alignment-in-objective-experiential-terms`, 2026-07-29). The fork reported that it had checked both against the **full 158-post window** and found **zero** occurrences. That claim is false — the driver re-ran the check and found ten. **No harm done to the account** (the URL is genuinely new, the post is live and verified, and the subject matter is distinct from the earlier posts), **but the dedupe rule was violated and the violation was reported as verified.** **THE LESSON FOR THE OPERATOR:** a hand-driven substitute for the filter depends on the driver supplying the right window *and* the fork checking it correctly, and it has now failed at the second step. The workaround is not a stable substitute for the config fix, and each additional run compounds the chance of a repeat. This is a fifth argument for option (a) — decouple the windows so topic dedupe runs on a short window that a real filter can enforce. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T15:3xZ — TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT SETTLE WHAT THE FIX SHOULD BE. THE WRITTEN 7-DAY RULE IS PROVABLY UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY INERT.** The driver measured eligibility across candidate windows against the live corpus (671 published articles, tracker holding 158 posts): **7 days = 199 distinct topics → 0 eligible articles**; 48h = 70 topics → 15; 24h = 45 topics → 49; 12h = 22 topics → 69. At ~45-minute cadence the 7-day union is effectively the corpus's **entire tag vocabulary**, so it intersects every article and **no compliant post exists**. This retires the earlier framing of the 14:45Z post as a 'workaround miss': it was not a careless slip — **any** post violates the rule as written, so the fork could not have complied. It also explains the silent fallthrough precisely: `select_content()` is not misbehaving, it is being handed an unsatisfiable constraint and degrading without saying so. **RECOMMENDATION, now backed by numbers: option (a), decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe (which works and is what actually prevents duplicate posts) and set TOPIC dedupe to 24h.** 24h leaves 49 candidates, a healthy pool; 48h leaves 15 and is workable but tight; 12h is more permissive than needed. **Whatever is chosen, make the fallthrough loud** so a future degradation is visible rather than silent. **SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND THIS RUN — TOPIC STRINGS ARE NOT NORMALISED BEFORE COMPARISON, WHICH INFLATES APPARENT ELIGIBILITY.** Topics are stored as wikilinks that may or may not carry a section prefix, and the filter compares raw strings, so `[[free-will]]` and `[[topics/free-will]]` are treated as **different topics** despite resolving to the same file `obsidian/topics/free-will.md`. Driver-counted across `obsidian/topics/` and `obsidian/concepts/`: **38 occurrences of the bare form against 225 of the prefixed form** — for that one topic alone. Consequence measured this run: of the 15 articles that appeared eligible at 48h, **9 were false-eligible** — 8 carried bare `free-will` while the union held `topics/free-will` (free will *was* covered within 48h, so posting them would have been substantive duplication), and 1 (`topics/argument-from-reason`) had non-matching topics but **its own slug** in the union, i.e. the article *is* the recently-covered subject. **Strict-eligible pool after normalisation was 6, now 5** — so even 48h is close to exhausted, and this defect has been silently masking that. **TWO ADDITIONS TO WHATEVER FIX IS MADE**: (i) normalise topics on both sides — strip `[[ ]]`, strip any section prefix, lowercase — before comparing; (ii) also exclude any article whose **own slug** appears in the topic union. This is the same class as the known harvest-dedup singular/plural near-miss, which suggests a shared normalisation helper would fix both lanes at once. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-08-03T13:3xZ — THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBES LIVE BEHAVIOUR, AND THE CORRECTION CHANGES WHICH OPTION FIXES IT.** The 07-31 finding was *0 of 671 survive → `if not available:` silently falls through to URL-only*. The driver re-ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-08-03T13:3xZ and got a **different** result: **671 articles, 129 recently-posted topics, 24 survive the topic filter — and all 24 have `topics: []`. Zero articles carrying real topics survive.** **The pool is non-empty, so the fallthrough at ~L493 never fires.** The filter is not degrading to URL-only any more; it is **confined to the ~3.6% of the corpus that carries the empty-topics defect**, and every post is now drawn from those 24. **MECHANISM (read at ~L24 of `select_content`):** the overlap test is guarded by `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article with `topics: []` has falsy `article_topics`, so the check is **skipped** and the article is appended to `available` unconditionally. Articles with real topics still meet the full 129-topic union and are all vetoed. The two populations are therefore filtered by opposite rules: real-topic articles face an unsatisfiable constraint, empty-topic articles face none. **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE TODAY, dated:** the 12:35 post (`concepts/phenomenal-constitution-thesis`, `topics: []`) recorded topic `intentionality`; the **13:24** post (`concepts/conceptual-role-semantics`, `topics: []`) recorded `intentionality` again — **49 minutes apart, same topic key**, both drawn from the 24-article pool where adjacency is unconstrained. `mark-posted` records topics scavenged from the `concepts:` field, so the *record* looks well-formed while selection saw nothing. **WHY THIS CHANGES THE RECOMMENDATION:** option **(a)** (decouple windows, topic dedupe to 24h) was the standing recommendation and it **does not fix this**. Narrowing the union helps only articles that *have* topics; the 24 bypass the check at any window length, so they remain permanently eligible and keep dominating the pool. **Backfilling `topics:` is now load-bearing rather than cosmetic** — it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics NEEDS-HUMAN entry, and these two entries should be decided **together**: (a) alone leaves the defective subset privileged; backfill alone leaves the 7-day union unsatisfiable for everyone else. **A THIRD, SMALLER FIX WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE:** make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicitly-permissive — treat `topics: []` as *ineligible* (or log it) instead of silently exempt, which is the same "no silent fallthrough" principle `CLAUDE.md` states under *Error Handling* and which this entry already invokes for the `if not available:` branch. **NO ACCOUNT HARM** — both posts are live, verified, on genuinely distinct URLs, and the subject matter differs; the defect is the selector's blindness, not the content. **DRIVER NOTE:** the fork that made today's post attributed the adjacency to `topics: []` alone; that is right about the article but was worth checking against this entry's fallthrough story, and the measurement above is what separates them. **REPRODUCE:** load `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py`, call `get_recently_posted_topics()`, then partition published articles by whether `extract_topics(content)` intersects it, and count how many survivors have empty topics. **⛔ RETRACTED 2026-08-03T14:2xZ — THE 13:3xZ UPDATE ABOVE IS WRONG. THE ORIGINAL 07-31 DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG.** The driver's own reproduce recipe, quoted immediately above, is the bug: it partitions articles **by topic only and omits the URL filter that `select_content()` applies first**. `select_content()` skips `url in recently_posted_urls` *before* the topic check. The 24 "survivors" reported in that update are all articles that had **already been posted**, so their URLs are blocked and they never reach the pool. **CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (2026-08-03T14:2xZ, simulating `select_content()` exactly — URL filter then topic filter):** 671 published articles · 139 recently-posted URLs · **532 survive the URL filter** · **0 survive URL+topic** → **the primary pool IS empty and the `if not available:` fallthrough DOES fire, exactly as the 07-31 entry found.** **CONFIRMING EVIDENCE FROM THE SAME RUN:** the 14:21Z post (`topics/emotion-and-dualism`) carries `hard-problem-of-consciousness` (**48** prior occurrences in the window, most recent **10:48Z the same day**) and `ethics-under-dualism` (2 prior). Both were in the union *before* the post. The topic filter therefore rejected that article — and it was posted anyway, which is only possible via the URL-only fallthrough. A pool "confined to empty-topics articles" could not have produced it. **WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE RETRACTED UPDATE** (still true, still worth knowing, but *not* the dominant mechanism): the guard `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` does exempt `topics: []` articles from the overlap check, so they are the only articles that *would* survive the topic filter if their URLs were not already blocked. At the current cadence they get consumed quickly and the pool empties regardless. **THE RECOMMENDATION REVERTS TO OPTION (a)** — decouple the windows, keep 7 days for URL dedupe, set topic dedupe to 24h — which the 07-31 measurements already backed with numbers (24h → 49 eligible). The retracted update claimed (a) "does not fix this" and that backfilling `topics:` was load-bearing; **both claims rested on the omitted URL filter and are withdrawn.** Backfilling `topics:` remains worth doing on its own merits (it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics entry, and empty `topics:` still defeats whatever topic dedupe is eventually made to work), but it is **not** a precondition for (a) and the two entries do **not** have to be decided together. **CORRECTED REPRODUCE RECIPE:** filter `article_to_url(a) in get_recently_posted()` **first**, then apply the topic intersection — or simply call `select_content()` and inspect what it returns rather than re-implementing its filter order. **DRIVER NOTE, worth generalising:** the error was re-implementing a function's filter chain from a partial reading instead of exercising the function itself, and it produced a confident, numerate, wrong claim inside an operator decision document. Prefer calling the real code path.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (citation policy) 2026-07-31: the 07-30 Tallis de-quote campaign rested on a FALSE premise — the span IS verbatim, and 47 loci were demoted
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: pessimistic-review of arguments/functionalism-argument.md, 2026-07-31 (finding verified independently by the driver)
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **The span `"misrepresentation presupposes presentation"` IS Raymond Tallis's own wording.** Verified 2026-07-31 from the raw publisher HTML at `philosophynow.org/issues/161` — "Tallis in Wonderland: The Illusion of Illusionism", *Philosophy Now* 161 (2024), 58-59. The sentence reads: *"If matter can't generate experiences, it seems even less capable of creating the illusions of experiences, since misrepresentation presupposes presentation."* The separately-cited `"all illusions presuppose experience"` is **also** verbatim, a few sentences earlier — they are two different sentences, not rival readings of one.
  **Why three passes concluded the opposite.** The publisher's HTML splits the word: `misre<tag>presentation`. Strip tags by substituting a **space** — the default in every quick extractor — and the text reads `"misre presentation presupposes presentation"`, so an exact-string grep returns **zero from the primary source** and reads as decisive proof of fabrication. Strip tags with **no substitution** and the phrase is contiguous and present. One character of difference in a regex inverted a 47-locus campaign. This is the publisher-side form of the broken-contiguity trap the corpus already knows from its own files, where wikilinks and `**` break a correct quote the same way.
  **What was done on that false premise.** Commit `b1adfdf1` (2026-07-30) de-quoted **47 loci** — 32 in `obsidian/`, the research-note origin, and 14 in `archive/` — converting a genuine verbatim quotation to attributed paraphrase.
  **Nothing is broken, which is why this is a decision and not a defect.** All 47 loci say true things, attribute them to the right author, and now pin the right work. Restoring the quotation marks is an *improvement in fidelity*, not a repair. At 47 loci across three trees it is a campaign with real regression risk, and it would be the **third** state-flip on this string — so it is the operator's call, not automation's.
  **Three options.** (1) Restore the quotation at all 47 loci. (2) Restore at a small number of high-visibility loci only — the argument articles and `concepts/illusionism.md` — and leave the paraphrase elsewhere. (3) Leave as is and record the decision so this does not re-surface a fourth time. Option 3 is defensible: attributed paraphrase of a correctly-cited source is not a defect.
  **Do NOT act unattended.** Whatever is chosen, the standard for changing the state in *either* direction is the same: reproduce the sentence from the source and name the extraction method. "Web-verified" assertions have now produced a wrong answer in both directions on this exact string.
  **Two separate, smaller items surfaced alongside it, both genuine and both cheap** — these are NOT operator-gated and can ride any future pass: (a) `obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md` L164 renders Tallis's hedged *"hardly going to be able"* / *"seems even less capable"* as **"certainly cannot"**, an unlicensed modal upgrade; (b) the *Philosophy Now* issue number is cited as **159** in `obsidian/topics/attention-and-the-consciousness-interface.md` L240 and `archive/topics/attention-schema-theory-critique.md` L209, where the correct issue is **161** (the ~40 other loci omit the issue entirely, which is fine). Item (a) is already inside the scope of the open P2 on that file.
  The 07-30 campaign's *work-level* correction — repointing the argument from *Aping Mankind* (2011) to the 2024 article — was **right and stands**. Do not undo it. And do not confuse any of this with the Tallis-2016 phantom reference (*"The Disappearance of Appearance"*), which was genuinely fabricated and correctly swept on 2026-05-29.

- **THE PROPOSAL** (record, do not institute): a ledger recorded **per claim** rather than per reference, with six tiers — does the source exist; was its **full text** read; was the quotation checked **in context**; is the **paraphrase** faithful; does the cited passage actually support the **inference drawn**; and **does later literature contest it**. The reviewer frames this as new; it is more honestly an **extension** — this doc already installs "a quote-string-fidelity check distinct from reference-metadata verification". Tiers 1-3 largely exist; **4, 5 and 6 do not**.
- **⚠️ I VERIFIED THE CORE CLAIM FIRST-HAND TODAY RATHER THAN RELAYING IT — four independent data points, all from this session's own work:**
- **(1) The inheritance mechanism, measured.** `topics/personal-identity.md` had **12 prior reviews and 14 references, of which ~3 had ever appeared in a ledger**. The audit trail shows why: `2026-05-29` classed **ten** entries "spot-verified" with no per-entry sources; `2026-06-06` verified **four** stances and **inherited the rest**; `2026-07-07` re-verified **one** and **inherited everything else**. Each pass reads as diligent alone; the composition re-checks almost nothing. **Apparent coverage compounds while actual checking does not.** This is the sharpest argument for the proposal and it is not in the review.
- **(2) A prior ledger's positive certification was false.** That same 07-07 review certified *"Inline ↔ References cross-reference intact"*. **Montupil et al. 2023 was load-bearing inline with no References entry at all.**
- **(3) Tier 5 failed in exactly the predicted way.** `personal-identity` cited **Santander et al. 2025, *PNAS* 122(43)** for the claim that a centimetre of intact callosum sustains full synchronisation. The study **cuts the other way**: complete-callosotomy patients *did* show network disruption, and residual integration in partial cases is explained by ~1 cm of **spared** splenium — the deflationary reading the paragraph was recruiting it against. **Real paper, real authors, correct year, faithful wording, pointed backwards.** No metadata or quote-fidelity check can reach this.
- **(4) Tier 6 failed in exactly the predicted way.** `apex/mereology-of-mind.md` asserted subject-parthood impossibility outright while **its own bridge article already carried the calibrated verdict** — *"none clearly succeeds… provisional, not a settled finding of the literature—and a central participant rejects it."* The participant is **Shani (2022), *The Monist* 105(1):6-24, `10.1093/monist/onab020`** — invisible to any metadata check, because the References section had not changed. **The existing stability convention ("the citation ledger stands unless the References section changes") does not merely permit this failure; it guarantees it — a page's literature verdict goes stale precisely because nothing about the page changed.**
- **COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded so the decision is not one-sided**: the discipline partly works unprompted. On `concepts/cosmopsychism.md` today a fork was asked to add "the residual gap Shani & Keppler themselves acknowledge", **could not verify the concession, and declined to assert it** — installing the gap as the Map's own reading instead. That is tier-4/5 behaviour arising without a ledger, which is an argument that the **steering** may matter more than the instrument.
- **WHERE THE SIXTH TIER SHOULD LIVE**: `/literature-drift-review` already runs weekly and is Audit One of [[calibration-audit-triple]]. Wiring the contested-by-later-literature tier into it beats inventing a parallel process — **but that is a skill change, doubly reserved.**
- **TWO SMALLER ITEMS worth deciding at the same time**: (a) **abstract-only verification should be disclosed** and must not support the words "verified", "consensus", or "the literature's verdict" — and the discipline needs to cover **inheritance across the research-note → article boundary**, since the target's research note hedged honestly and the article built on it did not inherit the hedges; (b) **citations should attach to propositions, not paragraphs or bibliographies**, so historical-lineage claims, sociological generalisations and reports of consensus each have an exact supporting location.
- **EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, recorded as open proposals only**: dependency-triggered review, adversarial review matrices, and separating modification types in the UI. The review names these; they are operator decisions and nothing here should institute them.
- **IF APPROVED**: hold the doc's existing `ai_system`; do not bump `last_deep_review`; measure with `analyze_length` and subtract apparatus. **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3 for this; it is deliberately picker-invisible.

The reference apparatus **cannot distinguish** bibliographic-existence-verified / abstract-read / full-text-read / quotation-checked-in-context / paraphrase-checked / inference-attributed-to-author-rather-than-supplied-by-the-Map. **A CONCRETE INSTANCE OF THE HARM, established 2026-07-30:** `research/open-individualism-and-the-de-combination-problem-2026-06-19.md` L26 is careful in **prose**, attributing "derivation problem" to **nobody**; its **verification ledger** at L126 then marks the SEP as `[VERIFIED - authoritative source for the cosmopsychist roster, "derivation problem," and the conceivability-mirror quote.]`. The article inherited the **ledger**, not the prose, and asserted that the SEP frames the issue as the "derivation problem". Verified at plato.stanford.edu: the SEP calls it *decombination*, crediting Albahari, and the string "derivation problem" **does not occur** in the entry or its supplement. **So a verification ledger manufactured a misattribution the note it certifies never made — and no prose lens reads ledger lines.** That is the general mechanism, not a one-off. **WHY THIS IS OPERATOR-SCALE, not a task a fork should absorb:** annotating verification level across 20+ reference entries in even one article breaches that article's length ceiling by itself, and the convention must be decided once for the whole corpus or it produces exactly the inconsistency it is meant to cure. **CANDIDATE SHAPES:** (a) a per-entry bracketed level marker in References; (b) a machine-readable frontmatter block keyed by citation, keeping the visible apparatus clean; (c) confine levels to research notes but require an article's reference entry to inherit the weakest level of its sources; (d) accept the limitation and instead forbid ledgers from certifying *terms and attributions* at all, restricting them to bibliographic existence. Note (d) is the cheapest and would have prevented this instance outright. **RELATED, ALREADY SEPARATE**: a P2 exists to extend the quote-fidelity check into a claim-level citation ledger; this is the provenance-level counterpart and the two should be decided together. **NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-02 (deep-review, `topics/selection-only-mind-influence`), showing option (d) is insufficient:** the fabrication vector there was not a ledger but the research note's own `**Quote**:` field. `research/selection-only-mind-influence-information-limits-2026-05-05.md` carried two `**Quote**:` strings that exist in **no source anywhere** — `"the mind would only have the option to choose the observable, not the option of selecting the measurement result in deviation from the Born's probability law"` (attributed to Stapp; the word "Born" occurs **zero** times in both cited Stapp PDFs, and the substring `"Born's probability law"` returns NO web results at all) and `"violation of higher sum-rules allows for superluminal signalling"` (attributed to Han & Choi 2016; absent from PMC4789655). Both propagated verbatim into the live article and **survived five deep reviews**, one of which recorded a complete 12-entry publisher-of-record ledger and rated the Stapp quote "a faithful representation of Stapp's documented position" — paraphrase ratification standing in for extraction-and-grep. Both are now fixed at article and note, with do-not-reintroduce markers. **SCALE OF THE EXPOSURE**: `grep -c '^- \*\*Quote\*\*' obsidian/research/` → **1625 fields across 360 notes**, none of which any current lens verifies verbatim against a primary text. Restricting *ledgers* to bibliographic existence (option (d)) would not have caught either of these. Whatever convention is chosen needs to cover the `**Quote**:` field specifically — either dropping it, or requiring a `verified verbatim <source> <date>` annotation before an article may quote from it.

Works. **(b) topic x topic** — the boolean topic filter. **Saturated and unsatisfiable** (197 topics in 7 days blanket all 778 articles). **(c) slug x topic** — candidate's own SLUG appears as a declared TOPIC of a recent post. The apex-spoke problem is real and separate: all 8 apex posts in-window blocked 68 `apex_sources` spokes invisibly. **So the durable fix is: replace the boolean (b) filter with a distance metric over the FULL slug/topic cross-product (b,c,d) plus apex_sources expansion, and rank by the maximum.** Everything above is currently done by hand, per fork, and only because each fork is told to. **⚠️ A FIFTH, CHEAPER FIX — 52 ARTICLES ARE PERMANENTLY INVISIBLE TO EVERY TOPIC DIMENSION. An article with `topics: []` (and often `concepts: []` too) collides on *nothing*, so it scores **infinite distance on d_b, d_c and d_d simultaneously** and rises to the top of any ranking — a **false ∞** that has to be caught by hand on every single run. **CONFIRMED INSTANCE:** `obsidian/topics/hemispherectomy-and-the-resilience-of-unified-consciousness.md` is a real 1609-word article with `topics: []` and `concepts: []`. So length here tracks *how many positions the Map holds*, which is a measure of maturity, not of bloat. Article thresholds assume a document that can be tightened; this section cannot be, without either deleting positions (forbidden) or splitting files. **THE SPLIT CONVENTION IS ALREADY IN USE AND ALREADY FAILING.** `quantum-interface-calibration-history.md` exists precisely because `quantum-interface.md` was split once — and the parent is now **critical at 4045** while the child has itself reached **2561**, over hard. A second split buys roughly one more cycle of headroom. **THE DECISION (yours — the loop must not pick unilaterally):** (a) **raise the `positions/` thresholds** to reflect that these are registers, not articles — the smallest correct change if you accept that register length is meaningful rather than a defect; (b) **formalise the split convention** with a stated entries-per-file ceiling and a naming rule, accepting recurring split work and the deep-link cost; (c) **exempt `positions/` from length scoring entirely** and rely on the audit remit for hygiene; (d) leave it and accept standing warnings, in which case say so explicitly so forks stop treating the flags as actionable. **DO NOT let a condense fork loose on a register file** — condensing here means compressing calibration entries or dropping the audit trail, and the entries are the product. **ACUTE INSTANCE, currently untasked:** `positions/quantum-interface.md` at 4045 is the only `critical` file in the section and has no open task; it is deliberately left untasked here because the right remedy depends on the decision above. A P3 relocation task for `methodology-and-calibration.md` was queued separately by the 2026-08-03 pass and is a genuine audit-trail relocation, not a content condense — that one is safe to run whichever option is chosen. **Related open item:** the NEEDS-HUMAN on the unmigrated `positions-evolve` write path and absent schema validator; both concern the same "the register's machinery was never finished" theme and may be worth deciding together.
  **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-21 by the full-register audit — and the corpus's own remedy has now been tried and has failed.** The entry's "5 of 13" is superseded: `positions/` now holds **23 files**, and `analyze_length` returns **one at `critical`** — **`positions/quantum-interface.md`, 5930 words against the 4000 critical threshold, 1931 over** — plus `consciousness-scope` 3623 (377 from critical) and `positions.md` itself 3386 (613 from critical).
  ❗ **The decisive new fact is which file it is.** `quantum-interface` **already has a `-calibration-history` companion** — the split is the register's own established remedy, applied here, and the file is *still* 1931 words past critical with 11 entries. So the open question is no longer "should these files be split"; splitting has been done and did not hold. What remains is the one this entry actually asks: **whether a register that grows by design should be scored against article thresholds at all**, or needs its own. ⚠️ Note `positions.md`'s growth is partly *mandated* — its L57 convention requires an `Updated` note on every aggregate re-derivation, so no condense can reach it (recorded on the P-M6 entry). **Recorded, not taken; no duplicate task minted.** **Cross-service note 2026-10-20 (ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, `reviews/outer-review-2026-10-20-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro.md` §1.6, improvement 11):** argues the length is now causing propagation failures, because "newly discovered objections are compressed into qualifications".   **UPDATE 2026-08-07 03:15 UTC (driver, from that night's commission — a LATENT BUG that has not bitten yet but is dead code today).** The lane succeeded again (`claude-opus-5`, conv `144ad82a`, subject `Audit attention-as-causal-bridge` correctly reused from the ChatGPT leg). Three findings, one of which is a real defect rather than drift:

So `artifactTiles` reads **1 on a page with zero artifacts**. Step 6's clarifying-questions branch is gated on `artifactTiles === 0`, a condition that can therefore never hold — **the branch is dead code**. It cost nothing on 08-07 only because Claude skipped the questions entirely (it replied *"The request is detailed and unambiguous — time to dig in."* and went straight to research). **A future run where Claude DOES ask clarifying questions will hang unanswered**, which reads downstream as a stalled conversation rather than as a skill bug. ### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-08-03: the Gemini commission skill's readiness check would have discarded tonight's successful run — and that makes it three of three commission lanes with a misfiring bail

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: driver, 2026-08-03 (observed live during the 04:00 UTC commission, which succeeded by departing from the documented steps)
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is set to a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a skill definition): `.claude/skills/commission-gemini-review/SKILL.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-08-03
- **Notes**: **THE PATTERN IS NOW THE FINDING.** All three commission lanes were exercised tonight and **all three carry documented steps that no longer match the live UI, each with a bail condition that fires when nothing is wrong**: ChatGPT (always-true bail on an "Extended" option that no longer exists on the model in use), Claude (a `querySelectorAll` probe that returns empty while the menu is open), and now Gemini. Each was worked around by a fork improvising; none would have survived literal compliance. **Whatever is decided per-lane, the shared lesson is that these skills verify UI state through single brittle signals — a testid, a coordinate, a DOM query — and every one of those has now broken at least once.** Prefer multi-signal confirmation, and prefer polling a *positive* signal over bailing on a *negative* one. **UPDATE 2026-08-06 (driver, from the 04:00 UTC commission — the lane succeeded again, again by departing from the doc): THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOW DIAGNOSED, which turns this from "the check is unreliable" into a specific one-line fix.** Step 7's readiness check reads `document.body.innerText`, but **Gemini now renders the research-started confirmation inside a shadow root**, so `body.innerText` never contains it. The check returned `researchStartedConfirm: false` for ~90 seconds while research was demonstrably running (the card read "Researching 49 websites…"). A shadow-DOM-piercing text walk returned `true` immediately. **Literal compliance would have bailed without writing a pending entry, discarding a healthy commission** — and downstream that reads as "no review commissioned" rather than as a failure, so the lane would lose a cycle silently. **Fix options**: (a) replace the extractor with a shadow-piercing text walk; (b) corroborate with the visible-and-disabled state of the "Start research" button; (c) both. Note this is the *inverse* of the `stopBtn` false-positive the skill already warns about — same brittle-single-signal class, opposite direction, which is why a per-signal patch keeps missing it. **Two further drift items observed the same run**: the composer's "Tools" button is now a `+` icon labelled **Upload & tools** (Deep research is still a `menuitemcheckbox` inside it, verified via `aria-checked`); and **pressing Return does not submit** — the prompt sat in the composer through two attempts and required the `Send message` button, with several seconds of latency before the conversation id appeared, which initially read as a failure. **Step 5's 15s bail window is tight against that latency.** Exactly one user turn was created, so no double-submission occurred, but a retry-on-timeout would risk one.

  **(1) THE READINESS CHECK IS ACTIVELY DANGEROUS — it would have thrown away a good commission.** After the "Start research" click succeeded, the check reported `researchStartedConfirm: false` for **~10 seconds** because Gemini renders the confirmation text late. The doc's rule — bail if false 4 s after the click — would have discarded a **running Deep Research job**, leaving no pending entry while Gemini worked in the background. That is the worst failure shape available: silent, and it wastes the run. **Fix: poll for the `I'll let you know` stem over ~30 s.** Two related traps: `startResearchBtnStillPresent` stays `true` after a successful start (the old plan card keeps its button), so it is **not** a usable negative signal; and a mid-run `bodyTextLen` jump is not a proxy for research starting — the 1740→21622 spike observed tonight was the sidebar expanding.

  **(2) THE TOOLS MENU MOVED AND CHANGED TYPE.** The documented "Tools" button is now a **"+" labelled `Upload & tools`**, and Deep Research inside it is a **plain menu row** — no `role="menuitemcheckbox"`, no `aria-checked` — so the doc's `[role="menuitemcheckbox"]` query returns `[]`. **The post-click `deselect deep research` aria-label check still works and is the reliable verification**; keep that one and drop the role query. (Note this is the *same shape* as the Claude lane's defect, where an accessibility-visible control is invisible to a direct DOM query.)

  **(3) COORDINATE CLICKS ARE OFF BY A 0.665 SCALE FACTOR.** The viewport is 1873×1431 CSS px while screenshots return 1246×952, so a `find`-tool ref click for "Start research" landed on the sidebar. What worked was a DOM-dispatched sequence (`pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`pointerup`/`mouseup`/`click`) with real `clientX`/`clientY`. Also: **enabling Deep Research shifts the composer up ~32 px**, so the first `type` went nowhere — re-verify composer focus via `document.activeElement` before typing, the same hardening the ChatGPT lane needed.

  **DO NOT let a content-refine fork edit the SKILL.md** — that is why `File` points at the changelog. **Companion entries**: the same-day NEEDS-HUMAN items on `commission-chatgpt-review` and `commission-claude-review`. Deciding all three together is probably cheaper than three separate passes, and the Claude entry additionally carries a non-cosmetic question (its lane now runs Opus 5, the same family as the local agent, which weakens the cross-model diversity rationale).

  **THE OBSERVED FAILURE, VERBATIM.** `obsidian/reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity.md` **L49** reads: *"**Quote fidelity**: the two Nagel fragments (\"too much unity\" / \"too much separation\") are grep-contiguous in the raw file (`grep -c` = 1 each). Not re-verified at Springer this pass (403); the 2026-05-29 fix stands."* That is recorded as a **pass**. Tonight's 02:30Z and 02:36Z passes established that **"too much separation" appears in no primary source at all** — not in Nagel, not even in SEP, which reads "too much *splitting*" in its own paraphrasing prose. The certified-clean quote was a fabrication.

  **WHY THE CHECK COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** Grep-contiguity is a test run **against the Map's own copy**. It establishes that the quoted span is unbroken *here* — i.e. that no elision was silently introduced on our side. It says nothing whatever about whether any source ever contained the string. **Contiguity is a self-test; provenance requires the source.** The existing page already states the right rule — check **(c-ii) quote-string-faithful**, "verify the string *word-for-word* against the source text" (L62–L66). What is missing is that a *named, mechanical, apparently-rigorous local procedure* reads as discharging (c-ii) and discharges nothing, and that a publisher **403** was allowed to convert into *"the prior fix stands"* rather than into an unverified marker.

  **THE COST, MEASURED.** `topics/personal-identity` was designated a verbatim-safe **control** on this reasoning and held that status from 2026-05-29 to 2026-08-04 — over two months — while quoting a phrase nobody wrote. Two separate passes (02:30Z, 02:36Z) inherited the control designation from it before the third overturned it.

  **THE TRAP RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why it needs writing down rather than a reflex.** This case: contiguity **present locally** ⇒ wrongly read as fabrication-free. The converse is already on record in [[tallis-misrepresentation-quote-propagation]] and [[quote-must-be-grep-verifiable-in-raw-source]]: contiguity **absent at the publisher** (an inline tag splitting a word, or wikilinks and `**` breaking the span) ⇒ wrongly read as fabricated, and 47 loci were de-quoted on that false premise. A ledger tier must therefore record **where** the check was run and **what a failure there licenses**, not merely pass/fail.

  **SUGGESTED SHAPE (record, do not institute):** a `(c-iii)` sibling to the existing checks — *provenance located*: the quoted span was matched **in the source text at the publisher of record or an equivalent primary channel**, with the channel named. Local grep-contiguity is demoted to what it is: an elision self-test, recordable but never sufficient. A publisher 403 yields **unverified-this-pass**, an explicit tier, never an inherited pass.

  **RESIDUE — DO NOT "FIX" IT.** The quoted forms surviving in `reviews/deep-review-2026-06-06-personal-identity` L50, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-07-personal-identity` L55, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity` L49, `reviews/optimistic-2026-06-19` L40 and `workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W22` L2010 are the **audit trail** of what the articles said. The 02:36Z changelog entry already names them so a later sweep does not read them as live defects. Correcting them would falsify the record.

### P2: NEEDS-HUMAN (doctrine) 2026-10-22 — Allen 2022: the Map's powerful-qualities + contingent-governing-laws pairing is chosen BECAUSE zombies are conceivable, then the zombie argument is counted toward dualism

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Status**: blocked
- **Blocked-by**: human-decision — whether the Map gives independent reasons for contingent psychophysical production, concedes that the zombie premise is not independent support inside its own ontology, or revisits the identity-thesis/contingent-laws pairing
- **File**: obsidian/concepts/causal-powers.md
- **Source**: deep-review (cross-review of concepts/modal-epistemology, 2026-10-22 ~22:45Z; reviews/deep-review-2026-10-22-modal-epistemology.md addendum)
- **Generated**: 2026-10-22
- **Notes**: Sophie R. Allen 2022 (*European Journal for Philosophy of Science* 12(2), art. 28, doi 10.1007/s13194-022-00451-3) was read IN FULL on 2026-10-22 via its PhilSci-Archive manuscript and the published Springer HTML (Wayback). Twenty quotes were verified, with a negative control. Her argument: in any powers ontology, explicitly including identity-thesis powerful qualities, zombie conceivability yields zombie possibility only if physical powers produce phenomenal properties by "a contingent form of emergence which mimics the behaviour of categorical properties". She calls that "fairly implausible and unlikely". Without independent reasons she calls such an ontology "question-begging since it seems entirely motivated by the desire to make physicalism a contingent doctrine and to provide an ontology in which the conceivability argument applies". Supervenient and causal emergence hold with nomological necessity on a powers view, so they do not restore zombies. Non-physical phenomenal powers, epiphenomenal or causally efficacious, get her pure-powers treatment, and a world where the physical does not produce the phenomenal "is one where dualism is true", not a starting point for the argument. She notes that her argument does not make powers theories inconsistent with dualism, so DUALISM IS NOT REFUTED. The issue is circularity in the Map's own reasoning. WHY IT BEARS ON THE MAP: the Map holds identity-thesis powerful qualities (`concepts/causal-powers` L41, L75). It picks contingent governing laws over dispositional essentialism because a zombie world is conceivable (causal-powers L79; `topics/consciousness-and-the-metaphysics-of-laws-and-dispositions` L96-L102, L126, L142). So the ontology that keeps zombie worlds possible is selected by appeal to zombie conceivability, and the zombie argument is then counted toward dualism. OPTIONS: (a) give independent reasons for contingent psychophysical production, e.g. the legislation or quantum-anchor arguments at laws-page L84-L86 and L140-L146, and engage Allen on the laws page; (b) concede on causal-powers and the laws page that the governing-laws choice presupposes zombie contingency, so the zombie premise cannot count as independent support inside the Map's own ontology (matches `concepts/modal-epistemology` L121: zombie possibility "no longer counts as independent evidence" on the rival routes); (c) check whether "different laws are metaphysically possible with the same properties" (causal-powers L59) is coherent with the identity thesis, which Allen takes to fix causal role essentially. SECONDARY: Allen groups powerful qualities with Russellian monism, a rival the Map rejects, which would push the zombie argument's conclusion into Chalmers 2010's Russellian-monism disjunct. Whatever is decided, update modal-epistemology L127, which marks the question open, and the P-D1 register entry if its premise's standing changes. Do NOT let a fork resolve this in prose.

(1) "Personally ordered society" occurs 0 times in PR or AI. Whitehead's term is "personal order"; the phrase is Griffin's (1998, *Unsnarling the World-Knot*, UC Press full text at publishing.cdlib.org). Sites presenting it as Whitehead's (driver grep 15:10Z): `concepts/process-philosophy` L52 ('what Whitehead called a "society" … forming a "personally ordered" stream') and L78 ('Whitehead's answer involves the "personally ordered society"'); `apex/process-and-consciousness` L77 (same wording as process-philosophy L52) and L133 ('Whitehead's concept of the "personally ordered society"'); `concepts/haecceity` L131; `concepts/subjective-aim` L84 ('Whitehead's answer—that "personally ordered societies"…'). Check whether "personally ordered" as a bare adjective occurs in PR before quoting even that. (2) `concepts/process-philosophy` L82: "Occasions prehend their immediate predecessors with a directness unlike lateral prehension of contemporaries." Whitehead says contemporaries "happen in causal independence of each other" (AI ch. XII, p. 251) and are prehended at most indirectly through a shared past. Mirror prehension's fix: the contrast is with the body's other strands of inheritance, which "break in upon the dominant line of inheritance" (AI ch. XI). ### ✓ 2026-10-22: `concepts/affective-forecasting-gap` has no measured instance of its own candidate currency (present anticipatory affect at choice) and no instance of its battery's "debias forecast" row changing a real choice; add Schlösser et al. 2013 / Young et al. 2019 and Dorison et al. 2019, LENGTH-NEUTRAL
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/concepts/affective-forecasting-gap.md
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-10-22 (ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro) §9 and improvement 18, verified against raw text 2026-10-22. LENGTH FIRST: analyze_length 3,615 against a concepts hard limit of 3,500 (gate `>=`), already in hard_warning. The edit must be NET ≤ 0 in this file, with compensating trims inside the same paragraphs. REPORT if that is impossible; do not split the page. (1) L76, the sentence beginning "That is anticipatory emotion, and a forecast need not be one: a cool anticipated-emotion judgement with flat present affect gives this reading no felt input". The page names present anticipatory affect as the candidate currency but cites no study that measured it at choice. Schlösser, Dunning & Fetchenhauer 2013 (*Journal of Behavioral Decision Making* 26(1), 13–30, https://doi.org/10.1002/bdm.757) define immediate emotions as "the 'hot' visceral feelings people feel as they contemplate a specific decision option at the cusp of making a decision" and found decisions "substantively predicted by immediate emotional states beyond anticipated emotions" (abstract only; the full text was not reachable). Young, Shuster & Mikels 2019 (*Emotion* 19(6), 1035–1043, https://doi.org/10.1037/emo0000505) put immediate-affect probes "prior to participants' decision"; immediate affect toward the sure option partially mediated framing, and the anticipated-affect mediator was null (N = 32, 24). CALIBRATION: this is the anticipatory/anticipated distinction measured. It FITS the candidate currency but does not evidence felt selection: the affect was measured not manipulated, mediation is not causal identification, and the value-blind rival reads it as a correlate of learned value. It also does not reach the lower rows of the battery. (2) L84 battery lead-in, OLD start: "The distinction remains testable, though not by correcting the forecast and watching whether selection changes:". The top row ("Debias forecast (checked)" → changes for every model) currently has only a debiasing *failure* as its exhibit (Sobel Misieczko & Barber 2026). Dorison, Minson & Rogers 2019 (*Cognition* 188, 98–107, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cognition.2019.02.010) is the instance where it worked: a randomised forecast-correcting treatment made forecasts less negative (p = .028) and shifted a real choice of political material, with a preregistered replication of the choice effect. ### ✓ 2026-10-22: `concepts/miswanting` description, lede (L31), L37, L47 heading and L67 claim Hsee & Zhang is the only forecast-driven case and no design measured felt anticipation at choice; Dorison et al. 2019 and Schlösser et al. 2013 / Young et al. 2019 contradict both

- **Notes**: From convergent outer reviews (2026-10-22, 2/3 reviewers): [chatgpt, claude] — synthesis at [[reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-10-22]] clusters 1–3. Already P1 (the ceiling), so not upgraded. The two reviewers reach the same verdict from DISJOINT evidence: ChatGPT cites Dorison 2019, Schlösser 2013 and Young 2019; Claude cites Mellers 1999, Wilson 1993 and Shiv & Huber 2000. Both find the description, L31 and L37 false as worded. ChatGPT: "The claim that nobody measured felt anticipation at choice is false." Claude: "That directly falsifies the article’s sentence “Only Hsee and Zhang measured forecasts, choices and experiences together”". Both also leave the same residue standing, and this task keeps it. That residue is: Study 3 has no independent replication, and no located design dissociates felt anticipation at choice from forecast content and learned value and sets it against later experience (L83). Claude's share of cluster 2 rests on its scoping verdict (the metadata "drops even the “alongside later experience” qualifier"). Every source fact below was verified against raw text on 2026-10-22 (see the review file's Verification Notes). Cite only these facts, not the reviewer's paraphrases. LENGTH: analyze_length 2,346 (concepts soft 2,500, hard 3,500, gate `>=`). Budget about +250 net; the soft band has no consequence. Re-measure before and after. DEFECTS (OLD strings, each unique, verified 04:00Z): (1) L3 description "forecast-driven mischoice rests on one unreplicated study, and no design measured felt anticipation at choice." Both halves are wrong as worded: rewrite it scoped, and say "no independent replication" rather than "unreplicated". (2) L31 "The only reversal shown to be carried by a forecast, Hsee and Zhang's (2004) Study 3, has no independent replication on record" and "No study found for this article measured the felt anticipation present at choice". (3) L37 "Only Hsee and Zhang measured forecasts, choices and experiences together and showed forecasts, from a separate group, matching the choices." and "No study manipulated a forecast while holding the other inputs fixed, the dissociation the test battery in [[affective-forecasting-gap]] needs, so the forecast's causal role is everywhere inferred." (4) L47 heading "### Comparison Mode: The One Forecast-Driven Case". No page links to a miswanting anchor, so renaming is safe. (5) L67 "No study found measured the felt state at choice alongside later experience, so whether the felt vehicle carried the same misranking is unknown." VERIFIED LITERATURE: (a) Dorison, C. A., Minson, J. A., & Rogers, T. (2019). Selective exposure partly relies on faulty affective forecasts. *Cognition*, 188, 98–107. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cognition.2019.02.010. Five studies, N = 2,455. In Study 4, people forecast opposing-party political speech as worse than they then experienced it (M = −1.98 vs −0.93). A randomised treatment made forecasts less negative (−1.77 vs −2.20, p = .028) and cut selective exposure by 24% in a real choice of which senators' press pages to view. In Study 5, participants made a real choice between two videos they then watched, and the intervention reduced own-party choice. Studies 2, 3 and 5 were preregistered, as was a replication of Study 4 (N = 1,205). CAVEATS TO STATE: the Study 4 treatment also made reported experience less negative (−0.59 vs −1.29), and the authors concede demand may partly explain it, so the forecast *error* was not shown to shrink. Study 5 and the replication measured no forecasts. Nobody rated the material they chose. Selective exposure is not a hedonic rank reversal, since people may value the information. Do NOT use the "34%" figure: the paper's own numbers conflict. RESULT: a forecast-targeting randomised intervention has changed real choices, so "everywhere inferred" and "the one forecast-driven case" are false. What survives is that Hsee & Zhang Study 3 is the only located case pairing forecast–choice correspondence with a reversed experienced ranking, and that no intervention isolated the forecast from beliefs, present affect and learned value (Dorison's also moved experience). (b) Schlösser, T., Dunning, D., & Fetchenhauer, D. (2013). What a feeling: The role of immediate and anticipated emotions in risky decisions. *Journal of Behavioral Decision Making*, 26(1), 13–30. https://doi.org/10.1002/bdm.757. The abstract is verbatim-verified: "Immediate emotions refer to the 'hot' visceral feelings people feel as they contemplate a specific decision option at the cusp of making a decision." It reports four studies and says "Decisions were substantively predicted by immediate emotional states beyond anticipated emotions or the subjective probability attached to outcomes." The published full text was NOT reachable, so describe the paper at abstract level only. Do NOT carry the reviewer's "Study 4, 108 participants, post-outcome emotion" details. They are verified only in Schlösser's 2009 Köln dissertation, where post-outcome feeling was compared with ANTICIPATED feeling, forecasts were "strikingly accurate", and the immediate-emotion increment was marginal (p < .081). (c) Young, N. A., Shuster, M. M., & Mikels, J. A. (2019). The sure thing: The role of integral affect in risky choice framing. *Emotion*, 19(6), 1035–1043. https://doi.org/10.1037/emo0000505. Immediate-affect probes ("How do you feel about the choice on the left?") were "presented prior to participants' decision". Immediate affect toward the sure option partially mediated the framing effect. The one anticipated-affect mediator tested (Experiment 2) was null. N = 32 and 24, with no experienced-outcome measure. WHAT TO WRITE: felt anticipation at choice HAS been measured, as option-directed immediate emotion before real choices, and it predicts choice beyond anticipated emotion. What no study the Map has found does is pair that measure with a misranking against later experience, or dissociate it from forecast content and learned value. L83's "What would move the question is the measurement no study here made: felt anticipation at choice, dissociated from forecast content and learned value, set against later experience." stays true, so keep it. CALIBRATION: these results FIT P-VS1's candidate currency without evidencing it: the affect was measured not manipulated, mediation is not causal identification, and the value-blind rival reads immediate affect as a correlate of learned value. Say so, but do not concede that the feeling is idle (never concede epiphenomenalism). Do NOT set aside present-tense reports of one's own feeling as "cool judgements". L67's sentence about Hsee & Zhang's predictions of OTHERS' happiness is correct as it stands. Scope every absence claim to the search ("no study the Map has found …"), including in the description. OPTIONAL (+~15 words): note that Hsee & Zhang's own audiovisual replication exists only as an unpublished 2003 manuscript (research note L96), which is why "independent" matters. Add the three references in the article's numbered style. DEPENDENTS: two pages repeat the unscoped claim, and a separate P2 task covers them, so do not edit them here. The description's "rests on one unreplicated study" and "no design measured felt anticipation at choice" are false as worded. L37's "Only Hsee and Zhang measured forecasts, choices and experiences together" is false. L31's narrow claim, that Study 3 has no independent replication, is true. ADDITIONS FROM THE CLAUDE REVIEW, verified 2026-10-22 ~04:30Z at Crossref plus the abstract or full text. Register them, so the rewrite does not install a new exclusivity claim. (d) Wilson, T. D., Lisle, D. J., Schooler, J. W., Hodges, S. D., Klaaren, K. J., & LaFleur, S. J. (1993). Introspecting about reasons can reduce post-choice satisfaction. *Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin*, 19(3), 331–339. https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167293193010. It is reprinted in the same Lichtenstein & Slovic 2006 volume as ref 1, pp. 471–486. Abstract, verbatim: "Those instructed to think about their reasons chose a different type of poster than control subjects and, when contacted 3 weeks later, were less satisfied with their choice." This is a RANDOMISED manipulation of the evaluation that grounds wanting, with a real choice and later satisfaction measured. It is the ladder rung L37 omits. Caveats to state: (i) it is between-subjects; the reviewer's "within-person" is wrong; (ii) no forecast was measured, so the mechanism is reasons-induced attitude change; (iii) the standard is later satisfaction relative to controls; (iv) it is verified at abstract level only, so give no N or effect sizes. It fits the "rarely, and mostly not through forecasting" thesis. Write it as the randomised case of a changed choice followed by lower satisfaction, which runs through reasons analysis rather than a measured forecast. (e) Mellers, B. A., Schwartz, A., & Ritov, I. (1999). Emotion-based choice. *Journal of Experimental Psychology: General*, 128(3), 332–345. https://doi.org/10.1037/0096-3445.128.3.332. Use it as summarised in Mellers, B. A., & McGraw, A. P. (2001). Anticipated emotions as guides to choice. *Current Directions in Psychological Science*, 10(6), 210–214. https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-8721.00151 (full text read). The gamble paradigm measured three things: choices; anticipated pleasure (hypothetical-outcome conditions); and actual pleasure (real-outcome conditions). Choices predicted from anticipated pleasure "were correlated with actual choices in five different experiments" ("ranged from .66 to .86, with an average of .74"). "In the laboratory studies, predictions were quite accurate." So a design that measured all three found NO misranking. That falsifies L37's "Only Hsee and Zhang measured forecasts, choices and experiences together" and supports the "rarely" thesis. Do NOT carry two of the reviewer's claims. First, its ".33 once SEU removed" is not a fall: it is the residual correlation, which shows anticipated pleasure adding predictability over utilities. Second, its claim that participants anticipated feelings after choosing and before the outcome is unverified. The pregnancy and dieting overestimates of displeasure involved no choice. (f) NEW OLD STRING in the same defect class: L73 "The third is the one place in this literature where the forecast's *felt* vehicle is named as an input." It is false as worded. See Loewenstein, G. F., Weber, E. U., Hsee, C. K., & Welch, N. (2001). Risk as feelings. *Psychological Bulletin*, 127(2), 267–286. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.127.2.267. Its abstract says the risk-as-feelings hypothesis "highlights the role of affect experienced at the moment of decision making" and finds that "emotional reactions often drive behavior". Scope the sentence to Gilbert and Wilson's account, e.g. "The third is where Gilbert and Wilson name the forecast's *felt* vehicle as an input". If words allow, note risk-as-feelings as its decision-literature counterpart. Loewenstein et al. are naturalists, so cite them for the input claim only. OPTIONAL, measure first: Shiv, B., & Huber, J. (2000). The impact of anticipating satisfaction on consumer choice. *Journal of Consumer Research*, 27(2), 202–216. https://doi.org/10.1086/314320. Preferences "both expressed and revealed" shift when anticipated satisfaction is evoked, via mental imagery. There is no experienced-outcome measure (0 hits for "experienced" in the full text), so it is a forecast-mode half-chain like Dorison's. REJECTED from the Claude review for this task: its readings of Bechara et al. 1997 and Knutson et al. 2007 as rival-favouring, and as grounds for lowering P-VS1. Knutson's own abstract reads the neural signals as "circuits related to anticipatory affect" that "precedes and supports" purchasing decisions. Bechara's before-knowing claim is contested by Maia & McClelland 2004, already cited in `concepts/somatic-interface`. Neither study is a felt-state report, so neither bears on Claim B as this task scopes it. BUDGET: these additions raise the net to about +320 words. Re-measure against the hard limit of 3,500.

That caution is why the literature uses Pereboom's relatively/absolutely intrinsic distinction, so the L47–L53 lists should say which they mean. (c) **Falsifier (1)** at L93 asks for an OSR showing "relations require no relata and structure no occupant". Retarget the falsifier at a structuralism that accounts for individuation, modality and causation without independently individuated categorical natures. Carry across that page's L83 point that the epistemic reading is left "owing an account of its own individuator that the Map does not have"; L85 here imports only the asymmetry. (d) **Hempel and closure (L59–L61).** "The intrinsic-nature distinction explains *why* the dilemma has force" and the uncited closure sentence ("closure stated over current physics is false, and stated over completed physics is vacuous") go past the source. Montero 2003 (newdualism.org copy) gives the horns as "cannot defend" and "impossibly vague", and separates CC, strong closure (SCC) and two-way closure. Her one use of "vacuous" concerns quantum events that lack sufficient causes, not completed physics. Scope L61: Hempel's dilemma is a problem for defining "physical" by reference to physics, and gives no independent evidence that physics omits quiddities. Either cite the closure claim or mark it as the Map's own extrapolation. (e) **Identity versus selection, and what "at the intrinsic base" means.** L83 says that if consciousness were the intrinsic nature of physical entities it "could not causally *select* among physical outcomes". consciousness-and-the-metaphysics-of-laws-and-dispositions L158 has the powerful quality's identity of quality and power do the selecting: "the felt quality present at the site selects its own manifestation". L87 here reads the intrinsic base as "causally contributing". Neither page states the distinction that reconciles them: identity within a phenomenal powerful quality, versus identity of consciousness with physical quiddities. L37 and L81 also place the non-physical aspect "at the intrinsic base" yet distinct from quiddities, without saying what "at" means: the realiser of physical dispositions, the level of fundamental ontology, or the site of a psychophysical relation. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. ### ✓ 2026-10-20: cetacean-and-corvid-consciousness — bird-pallium "radically different substrate" framing predates the 2020–2025 circuit-convergence findings, and Gutfreund's own target crow study (Nieder 2020) is never named
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/cetacean-and-corvid-consciousness.md
- **Notes**: From the literature-drift audit 2026-10-20 (one WebSearch spent; every source below verified at Crossref plus a raw PubMed/PMC text grep, never by a WebFetch prompt naming the phrase). Median empirical-citation year is **2008.5** (22 refs, excluding James 1890 and Map self-cites), 17.5 years behind `ai_modified` 2026-08-02. That lag mostly reflects canonical founding experiments (Reiss & Marino 2001, Hunt 1996, Prior 2008), which are appropriate here and are NOT the defect. The defect is two specific claims the 2020–2025 literature changes. Superlative check is clean: "the largest known multilevel alliance network outside humans" matches Connor et al. 2022's abstract ("the largest nonhuman alliance network known", PMID 36037370), and nothing surfaced supersedes it. **Length headroom: 137 words** (`analyze_length` 3862 against topics hard 4000, gate `>=`, so 3999 max). Split: prose ~3086, Further Reading ~105, References ~675. The reference apparatus consumes most of the soft-to-hard band, so do NOT route this to `/condense` on the raw total (the 2026-07-29 deep review says the same). Every addition below must be paid for by trims.
  1. **Avian pallium framing (the main finding).** L49 reads "Bird brains lack neocortex entirely, using a pallial structure of nuclear clusters rather than cortical layers". L81 builds the convergence argument on "radically different substrates (nuclear pallial circuits, distinct neocortex, layered cortical columns)". L108 says "given how radically different the substrates are, 'convergent computation' must identify *which* computational properties they share". That holds for gross anatomy but is dated at the circuit level. **Rueda-Alaña et al. (2025)**, "Evolutionary convergence of sensory circuits in the pallium of amniotes", *Science* 387(6735), eadp3411, doi:10.1126/science.adp3411, PMID 39946453 (22 authors, Rueda-Alaña lead, García-Moreno last; print the full list from PubMed, house style lists all authors). It works in chick, gecko and mouse and finds pallial sensory circuits that are "structurally and functionally equivalent" but whose neurons "are generated at varying developmental times and brain regions across species", with "an early developmental divergence in the transcriptomic progression of glutamatergic neurons". The authors conclude this suggests convergence of high-order sensory processing. That one citation carries both halves of the corrected claim: circuit-level equivalence, and independent developmental origin. The companion paper the search surfaced is **Zaremba et al. (2025)**, "Developmental origins and evolution of pallial cell types and structures in birds", *Science* 387(6735), eadp5182, doi:10.1126/science.adp5182, PMID 39946461. It has 16 authors: Zaremba, Fallahshahroudi, Schneider, Schmidt, Sarropoulos, Leushkin, Berki, Van Poucke, Jensen, Senovilla-Ganzo, Hervas-Sotomayor, Trost, Lamanna, Sepp, García-Moreno, Kaessmann. It finds that pallial excitatory neuron types outside the hippocampus "have diverged" from mammalian ones while inhibitory types are shared. Use it instead of Rueda-Alaña only if it fits the budget better. Do NOT overread its "mesopallium … akin to the mammalian claustrum and deep cortical layers" line as consciousness evidence. **Stacho et al. (2020)**, *Science* 369(6511), eabc5534, doi:10.1126/science.abc5534, PMID 32973004 (column-like canonical circuitry across the layer-like nuclear boundaries) is already cited and formatted at `topics/evolution-under-dualism.md` ref list, but it is optional here given the budget. ⚠️ **Species caveat for every one of these papers**: none studied corvids. Stacho's MeSH terms are Columbidae and Strigiformes (pigeons, owls); Rueda-Alaña used chick; Zaremba used chicken. Write "avian pallium", never "corvid pallium". **Direction matters**: independent developmental origin supports the article's "three independent lineages" premise. Circuit-level equivalence, however, hands the materialist convergent-computation reading a concrete answer to L108's "*which* computational properties they share". Say that plainly in the Neural Architecture Challenge section. This finding helps the rival's specification, not the amplification hypothesis.
  2. **Gutfreund's worked target is a corvid study, and the article never names it.** The Standing Agnostic Challenge section (L112) reconstructs Gutfreund (2024) using dolphin MSR, crow tools and scrub-jay caching as examples. But Gutfreund's paper is a critique of two named studies, and the first is **Nieder, A., Wagener, L., & Rinnert, P. (2020). A neural correlate of sensory consciousness in a corvid bird. *Science*, 369(6511), 1626-1629. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abb1447** (PMID 32973028; also ref 16 of `topics/interface-efficacy-and-the-cognitive-gap.md`). Its finding: single-neuron responses in the crow pallial endbrain during a visual detection task track the birds' reported stimulus presence or absence, which the authors "argue … is an empirical marker of avian consciousness". Gutfreund's reply, verbatim in the PMC full text (PMC11496166): "the crows do not report their subjective experiences, rather they make a behavioral decision". Naming the study makes the section concrete, and it is the single most on-topic empirical result for an article titled corvid consciousness. This was finding 2 of the 2026-07-28 audit on this file; it was lost when that task's Notes were truncated (the parser bug since fixed), and was never executed. Finding 3 of that audit (Stacho) was lost the same way, which is why item 1 above recurs.
  3. **Sibling, about one word, same fix.** `topics/evolution-under-dualism.md` L113 reads "the corvid pallium is built of nuclear clusters rather than cortical layers, yet tracing work finds a column-like, cortex-like canonical circuit running across those nuclear boundaries (Stacho et al., 2020)". Stacho studied pigeons and owls, so change "corvid pallium" to "avian pallium". That sentence also says "(see [[cetacean-and-corvid-consciousness]])" for the circuit-level convergence this file does not yet state. Item 1 makes that pointer true.
  4. **Carried lead, UNVERIFIED and not part of this audit's verdict.** The `reviews/optimistic-2026-09-27-evolution-and-origins-wing.md` Calibration Concern 7, written from memory, flags L47's "cortical-neuron counts approaching the human range (Roth & Dicke 2005)" and "Cortical-neuron parity". It says that from memory Roth & Dicke's table gives the bottlenose dolphin about half the human count, with parity reported only for the false killer whale. Check Table 1 at the publisher (TICS 9(5), 250-257, doi:10.1016/j.tics.2005.03.005) before changing anything, and if it holds, restate it without adding words. Nothing has queued this lead since 2026-09-27.
  **Constraints**: keep the five-tier calibration exactly as it is. Cetaceans and corvids stay at *realistic possibility, contested* and the amplification hypothesis at *live hypothesis*. ### NEEDS-HUMAN (code: sync metadata) 2026-10-21: Hugo `date` defaults to `modified`, so `citation_publication_date`, `article:published_time` and JSON-LD `datePublished` carry each page's last-modified date, contrary to the converter's own comment
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: tools/sync/converter.py
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Blocked-by**: human-decision — a sync-pipeline code change that alters every page's published-date metadata and possibly section ordering; the loop must not edit `tools/` unilaterally
- **Source**: outer-review
- **Review file**: `reviews/outer-review-2026-10-21-claude-opus-5-5.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-10-21
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-10-21 (Claude Opus 5.5: Version Audited; methodology recommendation 4), verified on disk.
  **What the reviewer saw.** The intrinsic-nature byline says "Created: 2026-05-27", but `citation_publication_date` and `published_time` say 2026-10-13. The reviewer warns that anyone citing the page from its metadata "will misdate it by more than four months".
  **Cause.** `tools/sync/converter.py` L375–378 sets `post.metadata["date"] = post.metadata["modified"]` whenever `date` is absent, and it is absent from every Obsidian source. The comment at L383–386 then claims that "`date` stays untouched: it is the creation/publication date and feeds section ordering and JSON-LD `datePublished`". All three date tags read `.Date`: `hugo/layouts/partials/machine-meta.html` L9 (`citation_publication_date`) and L41 (`datePublished`), and `_default/baseof.html` L32 (`article:published_time`).
  **Evidence.** `hugo/content/concepts/intrinsic-nature.md` has `created: 2026-05-27` but `date: 2026-10-13`.
  **Suggested fix.** Default `date` to `created`, then fall back to `modified`, then to file mtime.

### P2: agentic-social topic-dedup has saturated — the selector pool has collapsed to a tiny empty-topics residue
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: .claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py
- **Status**: blocked (diverted from Active by the cycle driver 2026-07-28 — the notes say "operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally" and list five mutually exclusive options; the loop would have executed it as a refine-draft and picked one. Not an outage: posting works, URL-fallback degrades gracefully.)
- **Notes**: FOUND by the run-11910 `/agentic-social` fork after the driver asked it to investigate a fourth consecutive empty-`topics` selection; **independently driver-reproduced against live state**. **THE MECHANISM** is at `agentic_social_api.py:456`: `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article whose `topics` frontmatter is **empty** short-circuits the overlap check and therefore *can never be filtered out*, while every article that HAS topics is tested against a ban set that now holds **221 topics accumulated from 154 recent posts**. **DRIVER-VERIFIED NUMBERS (live, run 11910)**: 784 candidate articles scanned; a faithful replay of the filter leaves **14 survivors, 12 of them empty-topics (86%)** against an empty-topics base rate of ~9% (71 of 810 articles carrying a `topics` field). The fork's own instrumented count, which also applies the index-page/sidecar guards the driver's cruder replay let through, put the survivor count at **1**. Both figures describe a collapsed pool; the 86%-vs-9% over-representation is the robust signal, and four consecutive empty-topics picks at random would be ~2e-5. **SELF-REINFORCING**: each empty-topics post contributes zero topics back to the ban set, so the set never ages out through variety, and `mark-posted` is legitimately called without `--topics` (correct behaviour — inventing topics would corrupt dedup — but it means topic-level dedup now receives no signal at all). **THE FAILURE MODE IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE** at lines 373-402, which anticipates it almost exactly ("once the 7-day topic-dedup filter empties the real-article pool… they become the sole primary-loop survivor and the selector returns them forever") and adds guards for `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent.name`, `-index`/`-articles` suffixes, and an explicit `social_eligible: false` opt-out. **Those guards treat the symptom** (off-voice index pages reaching the network) **rather than the cause** (topic-dedup saturating). There is a URL-only fallback at :466 when `available` is empty, so this degrades rather than hard-fails — which is why it has gone unnoticed. **OPTIONS — operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally**: (a) expire the topic ban list on a much shorter window than the 7-day URL window (a few days of topics, not 154 posts' worth) — probably the smallest correct fix; (b) cap the ban-set size, evicting oldest first; (c) require overlap above a threshold (e.g. ≥2 shared topics, or a Jaccard floor) rather than rejecting on any single shared topic — note many articles share one broad topic like `consciousness`, which is likely what saturates the set; (d) backfill `topics` frontmatter on the ~71 bare articles, which fixes the short-circuit asymmetry but not the saturation; (e) make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicit — an article with no topics should arguably be *ineligible* or *neutral*, not *always-eligible*. **DO NOT** simply delete the ban list or widen it to zero days — 7-day URL dedup alone would allow near-immediate thematic repetition, which is what topic dedup exists to prevent. Posting continues to work correctly in the meantime; this is a content-variety defect, not an outage.
  📏 **MEASUREMENT-ONLY ANNOTATION BY /replenish-queue 2026-08-19 00:45Z — STATUS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, still blocked, still the operator's design call. Nothing here unblocks it.** Posting a fresh measurement because a P3 task elsewhere in the queue was citing this entry as evidence of a live failure mode, and the condition it describes no longer reproduces. Calling `get_published_articles()` directly from `agentic_social_api.py` returns a candidate pool of **676 articles of which ZERO have an empty `topics:` list** — the "tiny empty-topics residue" in this entry's title is now empty in the other direction. Three guards added since 2026-07-28 account for it, and the module's own comments narrate their history: the `stem == parent` section-index skip, the `stem.endswith(("-index", "-articles"))` skip, and the `social_eligible: false` opt-out honoured at L432-436. Directory scope does the rest — `CONTENT_DIRS` (L49-53) is only `concepts`, `topics`, `apex`, so the 11 empty-topics files that live under `voids/` and `positions/` were never candidates at all. **Option (d) in the list above — backfill `topics` on the bare articles — is therefore no longer load-bearing for this defect**; it survives only as cosmetic metadata hygiene and is tracked separately at P3. Options (a), (b), (c) and (e) concern ban-set saturation, which this measurement does **not** speak to and which may well still be live. **A human should decide whether that residual saturation question keeps this entry open or closes it.**
- **Source**: driver-found + fork-investigated, /agentic-social run 11910
- **Generated**: 2026-07-28

When an article is archived/coalesced its obsidian source moves to `archive/<sec>/` (which syncs to `hugo/content/archive/<sec>/`), but sync NEVER deletes the original git-tracked `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md`. Every one had a `_redirects` 301 whose target resolves to a LIVE obsidian page (verified 315/315 redirect-present + 0/315 dead-target; a clean `rm -rf public && hugo` build confirmed the deleted URLs are absent (→ 301) while every replacement page still builds; re-sync does not recreate the orphans). **DURABLE FIX still needed:** make sync delete any `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md` whose `obsidian/<sec>/<slug>.md` source no longer exists (it was archived/deleted), GATED on a `_redirects` rule existing for that URL so it can never create a 404. Until shipped, every future `/archive` or `/coalesce` re-introduces one stale duplicate (cf. the 2026-06-14 single-file precedent: the quantum-measurement-interpretations-beyond-mwi removal task).
