### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-09-07: the citation-ledger inheritance rule let two phantom references survive four publisher-of-record verification passes — evidenced, not hypothetical
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Status**: blocked (changes a standing verification discipline; do not adopt unilaterally)
- **File**: obsidian/project/calibration-audit-triple.md
- **Source**: outer-review
- **Review file**: `reviews/outer-review-2026-09-06-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-09-07
- **Notes**: **This is the reviewer's improvements #18 and #19, and unlike most methodology proposals from outer reviewers it arrives with a verified failure to point at.** ⚠️ **The concrete defects are already minted as executable tasks (one P1 on `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model`, one P2 on `project/calibration-audit-triple` L495) — this entry is the *policy* question only. Do not duplicate those fixes here.** **The evidence.** The 2026-08-27 deep review of `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model` recorded, in its Citation Web-Verify section (L53 of `reviews/deep-review-2026-08-27-psychedelics-and-the-filter-model.md`): "The remaining 23 entries are unchanged since the 2026-06-03 full publisher-of-record ledger (re-confirmed 2026-06-19 and 2026-07-07); that ledger stands." Under that rule an entry is owed re-verification only if it *changed*. Two entries in that unchanged set are phantoms, verified as such during this review's processing: reference 23 ("Timmermann, C. et al. (2024). DMT alters cortical travelling waves…", no such publication; the real paper is Irrmischer et al. 2026, *J. Neurosci.* 46(2):e0344252025) and reference 9 ("Hameroff, S. (2024) … Cambridge University Press", where the volume is Gao ed., **Oxford**, **2022** and the chapter title does not exist). Both were present on 2026-06-03 and therefore inherited, unchecked, through **four** passes. The same section's L47 shows the deep review *did* touch Timmermann, Mason and Lebedev — but only to trim **recitation redundancy**, never to check what the sources say. A third instance sits at `project/calibration-audit-triple.md` L495, inside the audit specification's own worked exhibit. **The policy question for the operator.** The inheritance rule is what makes the ledger affordable; removing it makes every deep review re-verify ~24 entries. Three options, in ascending cost: **(a)** keep inheritance but make it *tuple-scoped* — an unchanged entry is still owed a one-shot existence check of the (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) tuple against Crossref, which is cheap and would have caught both phantoms, while the expensive part (does the source support the claim?) stays owed only on change. **(b)** Additionally require, on any entry whose *body claim* is edited — as L47's recitation trim did — that the claim be re-checked against the abstract even if the reference entry itself is untouched; this is the seam that let an editorially-touched citation keep an unverified claim. **(c)** The reviewer's fuller #19: a literature-drift gate for fast-moving empirical pages, searching from the date of the last full empirical audit forward and forbidding ledger inheritance outright on such pages. Note the Map already runs a weekly `literature-drift-review` (Audit One of the triple), so (c) may be partly built — **check what that skill already covers before commissioning new machinery**, and note it audits one article per run, which is a different cadence from a per-pass gate. **Caution against over-reading**: the reviewer's own framing of the Map's review record is partly its own reconstruction, and several 2026 papers it cites are unverified aggregator chips (see the review file's `## Verification Notes`). The *ledger-inheritance* finding stands on this repo's own record, independently of anything the reviewer got right about the literature. **Related open entries** — read before ratifying, they may compose or conflict: `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-09-02` on binding status changes, and `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-08-06` on gates-vs-lenses (the same "does this become a blocking gate?" question, previously answered conservatively). **⚠️ CONVERGENCE 2026-09-07 — a second, independent reviewer now names this same policy defect.** The Claude Opus 5 leg of the *same* cycle (`reviews/outer-review-2026-09-06-claude-opus-5.md`, site-wide item #5) reached the ledger-inheritance finding without seeing the ChatGPT leg, and independently re-derived the Reference 23 chimera and the Lebedev misattribution that evidence it — so this is genuine corroboration, not one reviewer's hobby-horse, and it raises the case for ratifying rather than deferring. **Two formulations from that leg are worth carrying into the decision, because they sharpen option (a):** (i) verify the citation **as a tuple** — (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) checked *together* rather than field-by-field, on the reasoning that Reference 23 was a title-from-paper-A + venue-and-finding-from-paper-B fusion in which **every field was individually plausible** and only the combination was false, so a field-by-field check cannot catch this class; and (ii) state the inheritance bar directly — **a review pass may not inherit a previous pass's verification without re-checking the raw record** — with the specific diagnostic that *any citation whose components trace to two different DOIs is a hard fail*. That reviewer also names the structural reason the pipeline is prone to it: plausible metadata assembled from adjacent sources, then a Claude-on-Claude review loop that re-ratifies a prior ledger's "verified" stamp instead of re-deriving it from the artefact. **No new task was minted for this** — the concrete fixes are already queued and this entry remains the single policy question.

  **ADDENDUM 2026-09-29 (combine-outer-reviews — a second evidenced instance of the inheritance failure, this time on a philosophical quotation, at 2/2 productive legs).** Both same-day legs on `topics/constitutive-exclusion` found that L44's Merleau-Ponty "quotation" ("We are both a part of the world and coextensive with it, constituting but also constituted") is the IEP author's unquoted prose glossing PP 453 — and the ledger certified it: `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-15-constitutive-exclusion` L40 recorded it as "Verbatim at PP 453 (confirmed via IEP and independent secondary source)" and `reviews/deep-review-2026-09-10-constitutive-exclusion` L109 inherited that as "publisher-verified verbatim on 2026-07-15. **Not re-litigated.**" The stamp came from a secondary source and was then fenced by a stability note — the mechanism the 2026-07-29 "End bedrock immunity" entry describes. **ChatGPT 5.6 Pro** improvement 18: *"automated verification should fail when a direct quotation has only a whole-book reference"*; **Claude Opus 5.5** recommendation 16: *"flag any quote first found in a secondary source (IEP, SEP, Goodreads, quote aggregators) as 'quoted in'"*. The concrete fix is the open P1 on the article (which also corrects the 09-10 ledger); this entry remains the policy question, now with two evidenced instances (phantom references, 09-07; laundered quotation, 09-29). ### ✓ 2026-05-25: Acknowledge dual-process / continuous-signal-detection contestation in memory-anomalies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-05-19d Issue 3. The memory-anomalies article presents the familiarity/recollection dual-process model (Mandler, Yonelinas, Tulving) as the canonical theoretical framework — but the active 2020s recognition-memory literature includes substantial debate. Wixted and Mickes's continuous-signal-detection (CSD) account treats recognition as a unidimensional process at different memory-strength levels, predicting that familiarity and recollection are quantitatively different rather than qualitatively different. Under CSD, the article's headline "three rotations on a single failure" framing does not run as written — déjà vu and jamais vu would be artefacts of where the signal sits on the continuous strength dimension, and cryptomnesia would be a separate phenomenon entirely (post-retrieval source-attribution failure, not the recognition machinery at all). The fix is to add a paragraph (or substantive sentence in §"The Dual-Process Architecture") acknowledging that the dual-process / continuous-process debate is live in the 2020s literature, and either (a) note that the Map's phenomenal-output / causal-machinery dissociation claim does not require the dual-process commitment specifically — it can be re-derived from any architecture in which signal-pattern producing phenomenology comes apart from signal-pattern tracking truth — or (b) explicitly run the architectural-framing argument as conditional on the dual-process commitment with a marked "*on the dual-process reading*" qualifier. Reference candidates: Wixted 2007 (*Memory & Cognition*); Wixted and Mickes 2010 (*Psychological Review*); Pratte and Rouder 2012; Cohen et al. 2013. See `reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-19d.md` §"Critical Issues" Issue 3.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Add MWI counterfactual-exclusion checklist across agency, death, quantum, machine-consciousness articles
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-22 ChatGPT 5.5 Pro §2.F, §4 Tenet 4. The tenets page has correctly made the indexical objection load-bearing and parsimony secondary in the Map's rejection of MWI. That repair matters because Tenet 5 (Occam's-razor limits) would otherwise undercut anti-MWI arguments based mainly on ontological extravagance. Downstream articles still sometimes treat MWI as if it would straightforwardly fail phenomenologically or empirically, when the better formulation is: MWI can often provide a branch-local restatement of the data; the Map rejects what it does to indexical identity, actuality, and selection. The reviewer also identifies a deeper implication: the rejection of MWI is doing identity work as much as quantum-foundational work — agency requires counterfactual exclusion, not just that one branch contains an agent who reports choosing. Tenet alignment: Tenet 4 (Rejection of MWI); Tenet 1 (identity-side).

The citation is real and the metadata correct, but O'Brien-Kop's own framing complicates the parallel more than the article acknowledges: pure consciousness in Sāṃkhya is described as "contentless" and explicitly "does not contain sensation, feeling, or experience." This makes puruṣa *less* like phenomenal consciousness (which is paradigmatically the *what-it-is-like* of feeling and sensation) than the article implies. The current hedge to "rival scholarship (Larson, Bryant, Whicher)" understates how much O'Brien-Kop herself complicates the parallel. Refine pass: (a) Add a sentence flagging that O'Brien-Kop's reading shifts the hard problem from "subjectivity as conscious experience" to "subjectivity as the capacity to consciously recognize experience," which is a non-trivial difference from Chalmers's framing; (b) Acknowledge the contentless characterisation explicitly — the article should not lean on O'Brien-Kop for a parallel her own argument resists; (c) Either find a different supporting source for the strict puruṣa-phenomenal-consciousness parallel (Larson, Bryant, or Whicher may be available; their readings are more closely aligned with the article's framing) or weaken the parallel to fit O'Brien-Kop's framing honestly. Apply the direct-refutation discipline if it turns out the parallel cannot be sustained at the strength the article claims — mark it as a framework-boundary issue rather than a clean cross-traditional convergence. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 + calibration discipline (don't lean a convergence argument on a source whose own argument resists the convergence).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Rescope or substantively engage canonical convergence literature in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §1 (Scope misframing) and §4 (Literature gaps). The title promises "the epistemology of convergence arguments" — a general epistemological analysis — but the article delivers a defense of a Swinburne-style cumulative case applied to consciousness/dualism. An expert in epistemology or philosophy of science would flag the absence of: **Whewell** (*Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences*, 1840 — the canonical articulation of "consilience of inductions," the structural claim the article advances, and the Hesse–Laudan debate over how to formalize it); **Laudan** ("A Confutation of Convergent Realism," *Philosophy of Science* 48(1): 19–49, 1981, DOI 10.1086/288975 — locus classicus for the very phrase "convergent realism" and the pessimistic meta-induction); **Psillos** (*Scientific Realism: How Science Tracks Truth*, Routledge 1999 — standard contemporary treatment); **Bovens & Hartmann** (*Bayesian Epistemology*, OUP 2003 — canonical formal treatment of convergence from "partially reliable independent witnesses"); **Blackwell–Dubins merging of opinions**, **Gaifman–Snir convergence-to-the-truth**, washing-out-of-priors; **Salmon** on common-cause explanation (directly relevant to the article's "common-cause-null" gesture, see separate task on that); **Sober** on the law of likelihood; **Lipton** (*Inference to the Best Explanation*, 2nd ed., Routledge 2004); **Stanford** (*Exceeding Our Grasp*, OUP 2006, on the problem of unconceived alternatives — directly relevant to the article's claim that no rival explanation of cross-cultural patterns is available); **Peirce** on convergence to truth in the long run; **Condorcet** jury theorem; and consensus-as-marker-of-reliability literature (Solomon, Beatty, Moss). Refine pass should choose between two paths: (a) **rescope** — retitle to something like "A Cumulative Case for the Irreducibility of Consciousness" or "Cross-Traditional Convergence and the Hard Problem," which is what the article actually argues; or (b) **expand** — add substantive sections engaging at minimum Whewell, Laudan 1981, Bovens & Hartmann 2003, plus the Bayesian convergence-of-opinion theorems. Option (a) is cheaper but cedes the more ambitious framing; option (b) lifts the article to a genuine contribution to the convergence-epistemology literature. The editor decision belongs in the changelog. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms (Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction needs honest engagement, not deflection), naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement (the article's distinction between convergence-on-diagnosis vs convergence-on-solution may be the framework-boundary move that makes engagement with Laudan tractable). Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [[writing-style|the writing-style guide]]'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.** Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction is the canonical case for parsimony's limits); the engagement is also a calibration check on whether the convergence argument is doing the work claimed.

### ✓ 2026-05-23: Anchor the 613 THz finding to Craddock et al. 2017 across the corpus
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-22 Claude Opus 4.7 §Key Findings 8(b), §Details 4. The 613 THz anaesthetic-correlated tubulin oscillation finding is currently attributed across the corpus to "Wiest et al. 2025" (`concepts/quantum-consciousness.md` line 70; `concepts/decoherence.md` line 99; `topics/comparing-quantum-consciousness-mechanisms.md` line 74; `topics/empirical-evidence-for-consciousness-selecting.md` line 95), to "Travis et al. 2024" (`topics/quantum-biology-and-neural-consciousness.md` line 75), and to "Wiest et al. (2024, 2025)" (`concepts/consciousness-selecting-neural-patterns.md` line 56). All of these are wrong. Verified: Craddock, Kurian, Preto, Sahu, Hameroff, Klobukowski & Tuszynski (2017), "Anesthetic Alterations of Collective Terahertz Oscillations in Tubulin Correlate with Clinical Potency: Implications for Anesthetic Action and Post-Operative Cognitive Dysfunction," *Scientific Reports* 7:9877, DOI 10.1038/s41598-017-09992-7, reports the (613 ± 8) THz finding from molecular-docking simulations and quantum-chemistry calculations — it is a *computational prediction*, not an experimental observation. Wiest 2025 *Neuroscience of Consciousness* is a perspective synthesizing existing literature with no new data. Refine pass should: (a) correct the attribution in each of the five files listed above to Craddock et al. 2017; (b) explicitly state that the finding is computational (molecular-dynamics / quantum-chemistry), not experimental; (c) reframe "a testable signature, though independent replication is needed" to reflect that there is no original experiment to replicate, only a computational prediction to be experimentally checked; (d) where Wiest 2025 is cited, retain it as the review that surveys the finding rather than as the source. This is multiple vault-wide misattributions of the same kind and should be done in one sweep. Honour [[evidential-status-discipline]] — recalibrate the finding's evidential tier downward from what it currently reads as. Tenet alignment: Tenet 2 (Minimal Quantum Interaction) calibration; citation integrity.

### ✓ 2026-05-19: Write topic article on Memory-System Vulnerability Hierarchies as Interface Evidence
- **Type**: expand-topic

The hierarchy is one of the catalogue's most underdeveloped strengths: it is a *graded* prediction the filter theory makes ("an interface with multiple channels is partially blocked") that production theories struggle to predict (they would predict uniform loss). A dedicated topic article would map the hierarchy across (a) anaesthesia (anoetic preserved, noetic disrupted, autonoetic severed) — Tulving's framework + the anaesthesia-recovery literature; (b) sleep stages (NREM-2 disrupts autonoetic, REM partially restores noetic-autonoetic, dreams produce noetic-only narratives); (c) hemispherectomy preservation patterns (which channels return after hemispheric reorganisation; the surprising preservation in adult-onset cases); (d) terminal lucidity (which channels return in the last hours/days — the catalogue's strongest exhibit of selective channel-restoration); (e) dissociative states (DID's compartmentalised autonoetic access; dissociative amnesia's selective autonoetic blockade with noetic preserved). The philosophical work: graded-vulnerability-with-separable-channels is a *stronger* filter-prediction than the single-binary-extinction reading — production theories must additionally account for *why these channels degrade in this order*, while filter theory predicts the ordering directly from differential channel-bandwidth and reconstruction-cost. Should explicitly engage the rival predictive-processing reading (which can also produce graded predictions through hierarchical-prior reweighting) and locate the disagreement at where each framing predicts the ordering from. - **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Research completed in research/voids-erasure-void-2026-03-20.md (2026-03-20) and never synthesised into an article. Key sources in research note: Gertler on anosognosia and unity of consciousness, the TiCS 2024 visual-metacognition review, Alzheimer's metacognitive-error studies, the "unknown unknowns" / hypocognition material, and the SEP entry on epistemological problems of memory. Tenet alignment: Dualism (selective disruption of the monitoring interface is predicted by mind-brain distinctness but puzzling under identity theory), Bidirectional Interaction (self-monitoring has an architecture, not a brute given), Occam's Razor Has Limits (confabulation constructs the illusion of completeness). Category: Occluded/Unexplorable (mixed). Target section: voids/ (~93/100 — has capacity). Scope: 2200-2700 words. Cross-link candidates: [[transparency-void]], [[inaccessible-past]], [[self-opacity]], [[self-transcendence-void]], [[observation-void]]. Preserve distinction from inaccessible-past: this void is not about what has been forgotten but about the invisibility of the loss itself.

- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: Russellian monism (Chalmers 2015, Alter & Nagasawa 2015) is the closest competitor — both say physics describes structure while consciousness is "missing." (4) Does Russellian monism handle the measurement problem? Research Chalmers' "The Combination Problem for Panpsychism," Goff's "Consciousness and Fundamental Reality," Stoljar's "Ignorance and Imagination." Critical positioning work. Target: research note.
- **Output**: Russellian monism as competitor to bi-aspectual dualism

### ✓ 2026-02-20: Fix self-undermining meta-argument in consciousness-and-the-problem-of-theoretical-virtues.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review (2026-02-20 afternoon) found the article argues theoretical virtues malfunction for consciousness, then claims this is "predicted by dualism and anomalous for physicalism." This is inconsistent — you cannot argue theory-choice machinery is broken, then use theory-choice reasoning to prefer dualism. Either acknowledge virtue-failure is neutral between dualism and physicalism, or develop the meta-argument more carefully by distinguishing first-order virtue application from second-order reasoning. Also engage with mysterianism as a genuine competitor (cognitive closure offers equally parsimonious reading of virtue failure). See pessimistic-2026-02-20-afternoon.md
- **Output**: obsidian/topics/consciousness-and-the-problem-of-theoretical-virtues.md

### P3: Concept page on the argument from mechanism (sufficiency-necessity non-sequitur)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-08 (High Priority). `topics/out-of-body-experiences.md` lines 83–91 identify and refuse a recurrent inferential pattern in consciousness-debate literature — the move from "phenomenon X can be produced by mechanism M" to "all instances of X are produced by M" — naming it as a non-sequitur ("That a phenomenon can be produced by mechanism M does not show that all instances of the phenomenon are produced by M. Visual experience can be induced by direct cortical stimulation; that does not make ordinary vision hallucinatory"). The pattern is *portable*: it surfaces in psychedelic-experience debates (drug-induced mystical experience produces serotonergic cascade ↛ all mystical experience reduces to serotonergic cascade), in lucid-dreaming debates, in NDE debates, in dissociative-disorder debates, in religious-experience debates, and in many places where dualist-friendly phenomenology has a reductive sufficient-mechanism explanation available. A standalone concept page would (a) name the inferential pattern formally as a *sufficiency-vs-necessity* fallacy in the Map's named-discipline catalogue alongside `concepts/possibility-probability-slippage` and `concepts/evidential-status-discipline`; (b) catalogue the catalogue's existing instances (OBE, lucid dreaming, psychedelics, hypnagogic phenomenology) as worked examples; (c) develop the *symmetric* discipline — the materialist's argument from mechanism is rejected, but so is the dualist's argument from "no mechanism fully explains X therefore mind is involved", which is the parallel non-sequitur in the opposite direction; (d) install the article as a citable handle for dependent articles facing this inference-pattern. The Map already has the discipline operational across multiple articles; what is missing is the *named anchor* for it. Estimated scope: 1500–2000 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — interacts with Tenet 1 (the dualism-friendly inferences depend on the symmetric version of the discipline) and Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — premature parsimony is what the materialist's argument-from-mechanism move attempts).
